rows.text: 12 system hours until Charmony Festival - Astral Express
Newsflash: Penacony's Charmony Festival has entered its countdown phase. Accompanied by Clockie's tick-tocks, after 12 system hours, this grand celebration will commence with much fanfare...
rows.speaker: Male Voice

rows.text: I already told you! We can talk things out!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: I'm sorry, fluffy. I really have something urgent to attend to, so I had no choice but to resort to asking this favor of you all.
Since you already know what you're doing, I'll also have to remind you of its risks.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey pardner, what's with the hostility? I thought pulling this thing out was just a way of saying hello?
For the last time, state your identity and purpose.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: My name's Boothill, and I'm a Galaxy Ranger.
A Galaxy Ranger?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You look like you've seen a ghost. Did you think we all went extinct? Haha! Well, that's the price you pay for being off-grid for too long.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: The righteous heroes of The Hunt would never hijack the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I ain't hijacked anything! What, chatting with someone while holding a gun is considered a hijacking?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: It probably is...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Pardon my frankness, but there are plenty of rumors in the cosmos regarding the Galaxy Rangers' current status, and none of them are pretty stories. I have a hard time believing you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This is hilarious. The tale that this bunch of fools spin is getting out of hand — there's even a bit about the Galaxy Rangers being turned into gibbons by Dr. Primitive, and they're in some valley screwing around on swings.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Of course, I know you won't believe me. Which is also why, similarly, I have a hard time believing that you're the real Nameless.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: See the bullets in this gun? 9-millimeter, an eternal classic. I may need the Astral Express' help right now, but if you're an imposter just like that one... Tsk, then this bullet might just end up in my head.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I can't allow myself to be exposed to danger. That's just the way it goes. So, you all have to first prove yourselves... Huh, where are you going?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Recognize this?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hah? It's a... muddle-fudger... the Jade Abacus of Allying Oath!? The Xianzhou really gave this to you guys!?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: *confused* M—Muddle-fudger?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: This is the jade abacus gifted to the Express by the Xianzhou Luofu's General Jing Yuan. Its presence onboard serves as the Xianzhou Alliance's official recognition of the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is that enough?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Not bad, kiddo.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: ...I don't intend to do anything.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: That's not up to you.

Did you know? People who come to the land of dreams for the first time, they'll subconsciously stop to reaffirm that they're still walking on solid ground. And then, they will unanimously raise their heads to gaze at the sky.
Be it reality or dream, staring at the sky is instinctual for humanity. Since the day that the Golden Hour was completed, it's always been there, watching over every single night of decadence.
But now this night sky has been mercilessly severed, dyed with the mist of Nihility. And this whole event... happened within the course of a single slash of a blade.
A single slash of a blade... isn't really accurate. It was actually two blades, just that the second one was faster.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: That's not the point.

Many guests who weren't supposed to be invited have gathered at this banquet. Even if the Harmony is all-embracing, I have no choice but to show some of them the door... for the sake of Penacony, and the peace.
The Planet of Festivities has no place for you, a puppet of Nihility. Those who live in the shadows do not bear the right to tread the illuminated stage.
Speaking of living in the shadows, there's probably not much difference between us. It's only polite to reveal your true self, at least when speaking to others...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Penacony's Dreammaster.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: That's just another reason that you can't stay.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Whether you believe it or not, this is the real "me."
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: We are one.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Is this the "United as One" that The Family espouses?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: My mortal shell has long since dissipated. The Oak Family's one hundred and seven thousand, three hundred and thirty-six offspring are now my eyes, ears and mouths, spreading joy across dreams when required, and in times of essential need... exiling evil from this haven in my stead.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: From the sound of it, it seems like you're asking me to leave Penacony.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I am glad that you're an understanding one. Alas, I'm not "asking."
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: If you think you can.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Are you threatening me?
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Hmm... I ended it with a period. It was a statement, not a threat.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Knowing who I am and still showing such malice, you're not the first, nor will you be the last. This scene played out many times before — and usually, when faced with my questions, most people retort "Why can't I?"
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: The result has invariably been that they "can't."
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: You are confident, but be reminded: The Family is forgiving, but not weak. The chords of the Harmony extend across worlds — if you do not comply, when the blade is unsheathed for even a hair's breadth, you will never be able to escape the Eternal Centurion's wrath in all of your lifetime.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: One hundred and thirty-seven individuals: That is how many heathens I have exiled since I became Dreammaster. Among them, were those who once severed my wings, and those who immolated my body...
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: And here I stand again, about to add another mark to the tally.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: And you will die. I mean... all of you will.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...But that won't come to pass. I'll do as you ask. I'll leave.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: A wise choice.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: I wasn't aware there was a choice.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: To you, that surely is the only option. Please bear in mind, you and Penacony are of different worlds — those born on the far bank cannot seek solace across the river.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Leave, and never return. The radiance of the Planet of Festivities is overwhelmingly bright, luring in tricksters, wrongdoers, and criminals. But even the Harmony itself... will never welcome the Self-Annihilator of Nihility.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: And even more so, when this Self-Annihilator heralds the destruction of everything. Your strength is obviously a gift of the sleeping and shapeless, immeasurable and fathomless, like a tributary spawned from the abyss that brings death and sin to all.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Acheron... a befitting name.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Take it from someone on the other side of your so-called river: You know better than I do that Penacony has already deviated from the Harmony. Whatever your intentions may be... I foresee only one outcome.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Its future holds nothing but Nihility, just like all the worlds that have drowned in {RUBY_B#IX, the Nihility}THEIR{RUBY_E#} shadow.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I can't believe I received a gift from Miss Robin... It feels like I'm dreaming! Wait — I AM in a dream!
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: If trouble comes knocking on our door, we're not afraid to go to war. Rest assured. The Dreamscape's peace will be protected by the Bloodhound Family!
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: The Family promised they would protect the guests within the Dreamscape, but I witnessed a group of organic lifeforms making their way to the theme park, and soon after, a rip tore through the sky, and black rain started leaking out of the void.
rows.speaker: Intellitron Guest

rows.text: The Family needs to provide a reasonable explanation, or I'll take my loved ones and return to reality. I thought the Dreamscape was supposed to be a paradise. If it's not, then there's no point staying here.
rows.speaker: Intellitron Guest

rows.text: It appears the good sir has seen many great events, and it's true that an uninvited guest has unexpectedly entered the Dreamscape.
However, their target is not the ordinary guests, but the ambassadors of the IPC. The Family will certainly ensure that the safety of the guests is of the highest importance.
Miss Robin. I know the Bloodhound Family has already sealed off the theme park and has control over the situation, but it won't resolve the problem.
rows.speaker: Intellitron Guest

rows.text: The Family can try their best to protect their reputation, but as a guest, I don't wish to gamble with my life.
rows.speaker: Intellitron Guest

rows.text: But as you can see, sir, no innocent bystanders were affected in this incident.

Perhaps the Dreamscape is not as perfect as promised. But there's no place safer than dreams under The Family's rule. I believe you know this better than I do. If this incident happened in real life, how many people would be able to walk away from it?

I could stay here. But keep in mind, guests come to Penacony to enjoy the Dreamscapes. They do not wish to be entangled in a conflict between The Family and the IPC so, let's not have any more unnecessary incidents.
rows.speaker: Intellitron Guest

rows.text: Of course. With the Charmony Festival about to commence, we will spare no effort in our preparations, rest assured. To express our apologies, The Family has arranged this gift for the guests. Thank you for understanding.
Hello. May I ask what happened here?
Nothing to be worried about. There's been a small rehearsal mishap at Clock Studios Theme Park. Please stay calm...
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Hey! Are you a fool? You don't even recognize Miss Robin? Who do you think you're talking to?
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Ah? I—I—I—I'm sorry! I've just been transferred to the Bloodhound Family, and I'm still not too used to working on the streets. I didn't realize it was you... I'm so sorry!
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Hey, don't sweat it. You guys have a tough job, I know how it is. How's the situation looking?
We've sealed off the theme park. Most guests are used to bizarre phenomena in the Dreamscape, and so far, no threats have been detected. We can expect order to be restored soon.
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Rest assured, Miss Robin, we'll intensify our patrols to ensure that no incidents occur.
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: I trust you guys. But... regarding what happened in the theme park, what do you Hounds think about it? It's okay. Feel free to speak your mind.
Well...
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Actually, I was there shortly after it happened... Is it true that the IPC's ambassadors came with ill intent? And that Galaxy Ranger who easily cut through the sky...
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Miss Robin, to tell you the truth, everyone has been talking about it. The myriad factions on Penacony have already been causing unease for everyone...
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Thank you all for your loyalty towards The Family. The Planet of Festivities has indeed run into some trouble. The representative from the IPC... He's trying to regain ownership of Penacony, and is prepared for a hostile takeover.
Of course, The Family did not agree. The result of the failed negotiations... is as you see it now.
No wonder. So this is the main reason why the IPC staff are banned from entering the Dreamscape. Did they apprehend the troublemaker in the end?
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Don't worry. Mr. Sunday is currently tracking his whereabouts and he'll have something to show for it soon. However, given the situation, the IPC surely won't let this go easily. Therefore, we are relying on you Hounds to maintain the order and stability of the Dreamscape.
Please be assured, Miss Robin, we take our orders seriously. We won't let those IPC cronies get away with this!
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Thank you for your hard work. If there are any other members who still feel uneasy, please tell them on my behalf that protecting the Dreamscape requires everyone's help.
This is a small gift prepared by the Iris Family for the guests — there's one for you too. Please open it at the Charmony Festival for an unexpected surprise!
I can't believe I received a gift from Miss Robin... It feels like I'm dreaming! Wait — I AM in a dream!
rows.speaker: Rookie Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: If trouble comes knocking on our door, we're not afraid to go to war. Rest assured. The Dreamscape's peace will be protected by the Bloodhound Family!
rows.speaker: Veteran Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: We're back to where it all began. You entered the Golden Hour from this place, and it is also from here where you will enter the true {RUBY_B#Land of the Exiles}Penacony{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It's a pleasure to journey alongside you once more, but it's time I laid bare the entire truth before you. As you might have heard... I also go by another name: Stellaron Hunter, Sam.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm fine... Sorry, I hope I haven't scared you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Welcome to heaven... dreams, true or false... all are ephemeral...
rows.speaker: Muddled Vagrant

rows.text: Might as well drink more SoulGlad instead...
rows.speaker: Muddled Vagrant

rows.text: Did you also get kicked out of the beautiful dream? I want to go back... but then, I don't want to go back.
rows.speaker: Melancholic Vagrant

rows.text: Tell me what I should do. Oh... I don't know what to do...
rows.speaker: Melancholic Vagrant

rows.text: Hi there, friend from a distant land!
rows.speaker: Happy Vagrant

rows.text: I hear the Watchmaker's Legacy is right here! Let's say we go treasure hunting?
rows.speaker: Happy Vagrant

rows.text: I'm sorry. I had no other choice...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I know you have many questions... Do you remember when we encountered "Death" in that strange Dreamscape? When I was caught by that meme...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: In that instant before it killed me, I saw the reflection of another Dreamscape in its ghastly pupils.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: So, following the clues in the script, I came up with some theories about the meme. That's why I instructed Silver Wolf to issue invitations, drawing everyone to the dream's hotel...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I intended to call upon "Death" before you arrived, to solve the riddle using more direct means, and then invite you to join. However, contrary to my wishes, I couldn't defy the script, and I didn't get a chance to explain it to you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It is how you see now — I was impaled by the bladed wings of "Death." The heavy pressure of concentrated memoria miasma... exploded in my mind, as if it was actually reality.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But after the momentary numbness subsided, I found that my body was absolutely unscathed.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I was still alive, and it was just as I thought — I had arrived at a place starkly different from this beautiful dream. Beneath the Dreamscape of Penacony lies another more chaotic, more primal Memory Zone. Its name... Land of the Exiles.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: And so then I returned to the hotel in the Dreamscape, hoping to tell you of its existence. Yet I could not reveal my own identity, so I could only divert your party's attention and lure you away from the battlefield.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: And after, all my attempts proved futile. It wasn't until not long ago, when a crimson blade of light shattered the high wall of the dream, causing you all to fall far into the abyssal depths of the Dreamscape, that I was able to awaken you and your companions one by one...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: And that's it, that is all that's happened so far.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I know it's tough to believe all this without reservations. I just want to say you're very close to the final answer — just one more thing needs to be done, and then I can prove it to you...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Now, let's leave this place... Please close your eyes.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Take a deep breath, and visualize the Dreamscape's outline in your heart. And remember... you must not open your eyes at all times.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Three...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Two...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: One...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Don't be afraid. The one who has come to greet us... has arrived.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I never knew you could do this.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Do you have a driver's license?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I do.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: That is... surprising.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Why? Because this is Jepella, the city of sins?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Mhmm, no... it's nothing.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm just thinking, you haven't slept in twenty system hours... Are you sure you're okay?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I'm fine. I'll survive. Same goes for you.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I'm not so sure about that. Slow down a bit.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Infiltration is over. Feel free to activate Sam anytime you like.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: There's still some time before the next part of the script unfolds. Let me stay a little longer in this body.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Such a long tunnel. Didn't feel this long when I set off.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: In half a system hour, it will lead us to Kafka, and then comes the downfall of the Jepella Brotherhood.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Is that also part of the script?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It's in your script, too.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Sorry, I didn't notice.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Their destiny won't change just because of your selective ignorance.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: I told you before, it's a bad habit.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: What about you, then? Is this the moment you finally find the "Death" you've been looking for?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: As always, it's a blank slate. It's not on this planet. Why the sudden inquiry?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Because I'm currently in a car with a sleep-deprived driver... I just want to get there in one piece.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: This car has full self-driving capabilities. I'll just put my hand on the steering wheel. Will that do?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Hey, don't take everything so seriously.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Elio would always say there's only one type of destiny: The inescapable type. He can see the future, and we... likewise are aware of our "predetermined end."
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But before that moment arrives, we can still choose what we do... We all have this right, don't we?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's your next stop.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Land of the Dreams, Penacony.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I hope you find whatever you seek there, be it answers... or salvation.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: [Trailblazer], glad to see you're safe and sound.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: "Close your eyes"... This is the answer. Isn't it incredible? The monster that we have always known as "Death," is actually the guardian of the land of the exiles. It abides by a certain rule, abducting people from their dreams and bringing them here.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The question that has been perplexing us — "Does death really exist in the Dreamscape?" — appears to be a cognitive trap. It was laid by those orchestrating events from the shadows to cover up the truth behind the disappearances, and the existence of this fortress known as Dreamflux Reef.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Every emergence of that meme is related to the Watchmaker. Since Dreamflux Reef is where it brings its captives, it's likely that many of our longstanding questions will be answered in this place.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The atmosphere here is starkly different from the beautiful dream. There are no regulators here like The Family, and they all look like they're mildly dazed.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But from the whispers of the residents, I've heard a familiar name... Gallagher.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It's that man again, always in the right place at the right time... though that does save us the trouble of looking for him.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Himeko and March have already made a move. [Trailblazer], get ready. We're about to set off.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: A long silence ensued. Neither of them brought up any topic, seemingly accustomed to this silence.
It wasn't until much later that a soft sigh once again broke the quiet in the car.
I'm really sorry for waiting until now to tell you everything.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Two reasons: Firstly, the script — in the future that Elio saw, Sam and the Astral Express' confrontation was inevitable. I tried to break the shackles of the prophecy, but this is as far as I could go.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That aside... there were also my personal motives. I wished to travel with you as Firefly... and not Sam.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Thank you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I... I get it. Being cautious around a Stellaron Hunter isn't a bad thing.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Elio only gave me one instruction: Allow the Astral Express to pursue the Grand Legacy. It means that the Watchmaker's Legacy holds great significance to Trailblazing, and to you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Elio's scripts used to revolve and expand around certain specific Stellarons. But with your appearance, this condition has apparently ceased to be appropriate. Perhaps, he also saw the "impossible" in the future.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Do you still remember the medical cabin I told you about? Well, that's Sam — It belongs to the Iron Cavalry of Glamoth's Firmament Frontline, a Fyrefly Type-IV {RUBY_B#S.A.M.}Strategic Assault Mech{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It is the cradle of my vitality, and the meaning of my birth. And for the longest time, it was... how I should have looked to the rest of the world.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The timescale of Dreamflux Reef differs from reality, so we mustn't lower our guard. You're sensitive to memoria — A slight misstep, and you could get lost in this Memory Zone.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Something on your mind? Let's talk about it.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No wonder Miss Acheron is so averse to drawing her blade... it's hard to imagine such terrifying power could reside in an ordinary sheath. If it weren't for the fact that Aventurine's power originated from the Preservation, the entire Dreamscape would have been affected.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Don't feel burdened by this. Even without that Stellaron inside you, Aventurine would still have found other methods to accomplish his goal. Let's just believe in Miss Acheron. And given her prowess, I don't think we've got anything to worry about.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: During your investigation, he shared a vital piece of information. Mikhail, the former Watchmaker who collaborated with The Family to construct the Penacony we're familiar with today, had a falling out with The Family for specific reasons.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: After today, Jepella's name will disappear from cosmic history, and the Ever-Flame Mansion will take its place. In the not-too-distant future, you'll receive an invitation...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: But this is precisely where the problem lies — you were clearly investigating a murder. So then why, as a security officer, is he changing the subject to talk about his past with the Watchmaker?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: And now with Firefly mentioning his name again... it's hard not to be suspicious.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Before we found you, she'd already revealed her Stellaron Hunter identity, and shared a lot of information.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: In the meantime...

Who would've thought that the Molten Knight's true identity was actually a young girl... For her, this is a secret that she cannot allow others to know. That being the case, I think we can believe she's willing to cooperate.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: But, she didn't reveal all her secrets. I just can't shake the feeling that her situation is different from that of the typical dreamer... And I hope that doesn't lead to any dangerous predicaments.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I hope you've regained a little composure. We'll move out when you're ready.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Keep going straight down this alley and it'll lead to an elevator. It'll take us to the center of the land of the exiles.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What a huge Clockie... Looks like the Watchmaker also left his mark on Dreamflux Reef.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Unbelievable... to think there's a settlement of this size within the Dreamscape... and all beyond The Family's reach.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The atmosphere in this fortress is... pretty different from that in the beautiful dream.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: When I first saw it, I was in awe too. The sky here, it's like... a reflection of the twelve Dreamscapes.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What's even more bizarre, is that this place is also separated into trade and residential areas. The layout may be simple, but the facilities are very comprehensive. It seems that there are quite a number of people living here.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Though both Dreamscapes have distinct styles, the architectural designs are quite similar — works of the same hand, perhaps. Hard not to speculate on the connection...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: But there's no point in overthinking things. Let's meet up with Himeko and the others first.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Take a right turn at the end of this road and you'll reach the trade district. There are more people there, and perhaps someone knows where she is.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Not coming with us?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Astral Express likely needs room for some internal deliberation. In the meantime, I'll try and locate Gallagher.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Sure, let's reconnect later.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Letting her go was the right decision — further observations are needed before we decide whether to trust her. But first, there's someone I need to talk to.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Let's go, [Trailblazer]. I'm sure you've already noticed him.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: After a piercing screech, a thick and ferocious surge of memoria crashes into your chest, churning and ravaging. Your consciousness becomes like scraps of paper caught in a whirlpool, breaking apart, dissolving, and dispersing within the turbulent muddy current.

Innumerable voices resonate through the symphony of memoria like roaring thunder, and among them, one echo stands out with exceptional clarity. You know it comes from the girl beside you, your hearts beating to the same rhythm in silence, and then, more silence...
Until memories stir up ripples in that quiet darkness...
He's right over there...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Look, over there...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hehe, not exactly — I've only met him once. Look, over there...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Reverie Hotel's bellboy... How did he end up here? And right after Miss Acheron severed the beautiful dream...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We'd better check, just to be sure.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ah? You're the guest from before. We meet again! And a new friend... F—Forgot to introduce myself, I'm the hotel's bellboy, Misha.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Hello, Misha. I'm Welt, we met in a dream...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Hm? And who might this be...?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Tick-tock! Old friend and new friend, let's high-five!
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: You're... a Memory Zone Meme?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Nope. Clockie is a good friend of mine. We all live here.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: How did you two get here? This Dreamscape isn't supposed to be open to the public... I wonder if it has something to do with Sleepie?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: So this is... your home?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yep. After my work in the beautiful dream ends, I'll go back home. Commuting used to be more convenient, but ever since travel became cumbersome, Sleepie started ferrying people back and forth between the two Dreamscapes.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: This Sleepie... Can you describe what it looks like?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Sleepie is a Memory Zone Meme, looks fierce and has many eyes. But it's actually really well-behaved. Gallagher's been taking care of it.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Based on the description, that meme is indisputably "Death." A nightmare for The Family, but for the people who live here... that couldn't be further from the truth.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: D—Death? Not in a dream, surely. Sleepie's just a little aggressive, and sometimes messes up by fetching the wrong guests, but it would never hurt anyone!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I see... Has it brought back any guests recently, say in the last day or two? We're currently investigating a missing person case that occurred within the beautiful dream.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I see... Then you'll have to speak with Gallagher. But he's currently busy hosting a visitor from the Oak Family, and specifically asked not to be disturbed.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Um, Mr. Yang, the person you're looking for...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Is it Miss Robin?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: ...Just as I thought. Considering what happened with Miss Firefly, this doesn't come as a surprise.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: If you're looking for Miss Robin, I can lead the way. She told me that she'd be willing to meet with outside guests.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: If it's not too much trouble. Also, we're looking for our missing companions: A woman with red hair, accompanied by a girl with pink hair. Have you seen them?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh, I haven't... But please rest assured — Dreamflux Reef is a small place, and it's not as bustling as the beautiful dream, but its safety is unmatched.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: How about this! Since it's your first time here in Dreamflux Reef, I'll be your guide and help you find your companions, and then we can all go visit Miss Robin together.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: She's gone to Mrs. Grace's to visit the children. She won't be leaving anytime soon, so there should be enough time.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Alright, then. We'll follow your plan.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Well, we now know the answer to both murder cases that have caused such commotion in Penacony. As for the intentions of the mastermind behind it all... we're still none the wiser.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yes, that's my thinking as well. I'm not entirely certain, but we still have to find him one way or another.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yes, and I believe their relationship with Gallagher may run deep — why else would they be so clandestine about their discussion? Regardless, we have to find Gallagher.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Uhh, no idea. But its connection to Gallagher is worth digging into. Regardless, we have to find him.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Say, you mentioned before that you saw a Clockie that only you could see, right?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I can't shake off this strange feeling. Am I really still so young at heart...?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Forget it. It's not important. We'd better just follow Misha.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Everyone, look! From here, you can see the most spectacular view of Dreamflux Reef—
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: A black hole? No... an accretion disk formed from consolidated memoria? Was Dreamflux Reef built on such unstable memoria?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh? So Mr. Yang is also versed in memoria dynamics. I was just trying to figure out how to explain this huge hole to everyone. I bet you guys have a lot in common with Miss Kaimee!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Look, there she is.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I'm Kaimee, a dreamscape surveyor specializing in memoria dynamics, and this is my life's work that I'm researching.
rows.speaker: Kaimee

rows.text: That's right. It seems like she did a great deal of research and calculations in Dreamflux Reef... before abruptly passing away.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Before we came to Penacony, the conductor had given us a list of Nameless to look into — her name was mentioned. It seems like she did a great deal of research and calculations in Dreamflux Reef... before abruptly passing away.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Miss Kaimee regularly mentions her. I hear Madam Razalina passed away during the Prison War... If she could see the Penacony of today, its people building homes in the Memory Zone... I bet she'd be really happy.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Let me go...
Please, come to your senses! I'm begging you...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ha. Ha. You're a regular comedian...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Me!? A ghost? Don't make me hit you!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He thinks he's dead... Although when I first fell in, I also thought the same.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: S—Stop asking! You'll alert the monsters! All the dead are right here, all of them...!
rows.speaker: The Family's Member

rows.text: He passed out. His intense negative emotions attracted the nearby Memory Zone Memes.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I see... but why aren't the other people around here scared?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Unlike in the sweet dream, people here don't see Memory Zone Memes as dangerous monsters... and even if they pose a threat, people can easily escape by forcing a wake-up call.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: But we can't just leave this man here... Can we take him somewhere safe?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: We can ask Jessie for help! I've gotten to know many locals while waiting for you guys.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Everyone here is living a self-sufficient life... I don't know how to describe it, but this place feels like the real Dreamscape...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is where we split up... She can't be too far away!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: An important guest? Who could it be...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This way, please. The roads here in Dreamflux Reef are a bit run-down, so watch your step.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: There she is.
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: It really is her... Miss Robin!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Everyone sang so wonderfully! It's not often that I try this music style, but I've gained some valuable insights from it!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I can't thank you enough, Robin. These kids have made incredible progress in only a few days.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: It was nothing, Grace. I merely taught them how to sing. It was you who brought hope into their lives.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...Life must be quite difficult for them in reality, I imagine.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That's right.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: Whenever it's time to say goodbye to these kids, they're reluctant to leave. But, I've explored every corner of Dreamflux Reef, talked to everyone I met, and they all told me the same thing... This shattered dream is not worth clinging to.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hehe, it seems you truly are a child of the Harmony.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: Emma and Andy are orphans I took under my wing. Carol, there, with her blind eyes, used to work at a nutrition center in the outer ring of Penacony. And as for Gary, he's been living with autism since he was a child. They're not old enough to enter the sweet dream managed by The Family.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: If we compare people to birds, these kids are like fledglings with impaired wings. But in this dream, they can fly freely. Even if they stumble along the way, they're still relying on their own strength.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: And me? An old lady with no legs... Without this dream, I couldn't even walk toward them.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: I'm glad that you found a new life here in Penacony, it's just...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Don't worry, Robin. Dreams have their significance, but they aren't everything. Both the children and I understand this. No matter how long we fly through this dream, we will one day return to reality.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: But you know what? Emma and Gary aren't plagued by their insecurities anymore. No — and Carol is learning how to cope with her blindness. And Andy is livelier than ever. Well, even I've become more optimistic.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: You see, in dreams, we learn how to live. Once we return to reality... we learn how to survive.
rows.speaker: Grace

rows.text: ...And should our feathers be damaged, then we share our wings with one another.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: There's no need to covet an illusory sky in dreams, because we have the right and the ability... to fly towards a broader horizon.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's a relief to see you safe and sound, Miss Robin.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's nice to see you all again, Astral Express crew. I heard my disappearance caused quite the commotion out there... I'm really sorry about that.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Since you're here... can we assume that you're fully aware of the situation in Penacony?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ever since I returned to Penacony, my voice started to change, until it gradually faded away. At first, I thought it was a temporary ailment, perhaps due to having been away too long. I thought maybe it'd just take some time for my body to acclimate to the high concentration of memoria in Asdana.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: But now it seems... the root of the problem goes way beyond me. There are elements around me that don't align with the Harmony... and losing my voice is just one of the signs of the sweet dream's collapse.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The sweet dream's collapse... that Memokeeper mentioned the same thing. So, it's real.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: While I was away from Penacony, the boundaries of the Twelve Dreamscapes kept expanding outward. But whenever I mentioned the anomalies in the dream... all the family heads refused to talk about it. Only my brother was willing to respond...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Later, I discovered the secret letters from the IPC ambassador, which further convinced me that there are hidden secrets beneath the surface of Penacony. So, following the clues in the Oak Family's dossiers, I found my way here...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...The land of the exiles, concealed by The Family under the guise of "Death," a dream within a dream where Penacony's past is buried.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hearing you speak, it sounds as if your voice has made somewhat of a recovery.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I hate to admit it, but the "Harmony" in this place resonates more broadly than within the sweet dream...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's regrettable, but The Family has experienced betrayal. The traitor, or traitors abandoned their original principles and, using the name of Harmony, exploited people's weaknesses to turn Penacony into the Planet of Festivities, trapping everyone in the illusion of the sweet dream...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This is not "the strong defending the weak," but rather "the strong exploiting the weak." A world without equality won't ever be favored by the Harmony, and naturally, those voices blessed by THEM... have lost the ability to sing.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Could there be another force influencing The Family's shift in philosophy, Miss Robin?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Considering what happened with Acheron, it's difficult to conceive of another entity within the realm of the Harmony capable of influencing everyone, unless a power surpassing that of an Emanator is involved...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'd heard about what happened to the Xianzhou Alliance. But as far as I'm aware, The Family hasn't faced any such external interventions. Who knows, perhaps I've just been away too long and missed something.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Regardless, I cannot accept my home is moving towards the very opposite of what the Harmony represents, while still claiming to uphold it.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I must uncover the reason why Mikhail cut ties with The Family, and who exactly it was who betrayed us all. Do you remember our arrangement, Mr. Micah? Well, here's my answer...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: — I've decided to forego my role, and never step foot on the Charmony Festival's stage again.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Look here, brother! A little bird!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Looks like a fledgling Charmony Dove.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But Charmony Doves don't live here. So how did this little bird get here? Maybe its parents abandoned it?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It looks weak and frail... Why don't we find something soft and make a nest for it?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: This place is too dangerous for a fledgling. Let's take it with us — we can put it on the wooden shelf in front of your window.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Okay! A bird like that must have a beautiful singing voice. But where will it live?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I'll ask the family head to build a cage for it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: A cage... but then it won't have the freedom to fly, right?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Let's see... what is it that has captured the attention of the two best interpreters of the Great One, to the point that they've forgotten how to enjoy their dessert?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: Oh... poor little thing. Doesn't look like it's doing well. Do you want to rescue it?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: I do... but I don't want to lock it up in a cage.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Why?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: 11 system hours until Charmony Festival - The other side of Dreamflux Reef
Even if it's small and not fully feathered, and can't sing... it didn't come into this world just to be locked up in a cage.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Birds... belong to the sky.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That's quite the romantic idea. And what about you, our young scholar? Do you agree with your sister?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: I think she's right... but if we leave it out in the wild, it won't survive for more than a few days at best.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ah, I see. It seems our little scholar is still a bit unsure. Well, let me tell you youngsters a story.
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: As you probably know, Charmony Doves can fly through the air. When they fly really high, the friction caused by the flapping of their feathers against the atmosphere creates amazing lights, so that they look like shooting stars.
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: We've seen this spectacle so many times that we think it's just something they can naturally do... but that's not the truth. Their radiant display is the result of countless struggles against nature over generations.
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: Their ancestors were too weak to survive on the ground. So, to escape predators, they started seeking new opportunities in the air...
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: After countless attempts by many generations, one of them finally figured out how to fly. It soared into the sky and never looked back at the ground again.
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: So, you mean, birds aren't born to fly, but they find a way to do it through their determination, right?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Well, that's an idealistic way of putting it. So, what are your thoughts, Sunday?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: I think people believe birds are meant to fly because... they've never seen those birds crashing to their death.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That's an interesting perspective. So, have you decided what to do with the bird now?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: For now... I'll keep it in a cage until it can take care of itself because...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I... I want it to live, no matter what.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Well said, kids. It seems each of you has found your own answer. Your insights are truly remarkable, and I hope they come true in their own way.
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: We will take good care of it, won't we, brother?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Yeah, but Mr. Gopher Wood, there's one thing I don't quite understand...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And what might that be, my son?
rows.speaker: Kind Voice

rows.text: What if this little Charmony Dove never learns to fly in the end?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I mean, if there are fledglings in this world that can never fly throughout their lives...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Should we let them go back to the sky... only to see them crash to the ground and die?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Talking in your sleep, birdie? Time to wake up.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: I wish that were the truth! But, if that were the case, I wouldn't have invited all of you.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: How keen! Well, what should I say? I expected nothing less from the person here who is the most familiar with Stellarons.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: The sweet dream doesn't come out of thin air. If you think of the Memory Zone as the sea, creating the land of the dreams is like filling that wild ocean with earth to make an island.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Ah... that line actually makes me a bit nervous...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Exactly! It's time for the Crew to save the world once more!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on. Don't crack jokes at such a serious moment.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Rest assured — sitting on the sidelines isn't in our nature. Mr. Sunday, Miss Robin, I'm willing to accompany you on behalf of the Astral Express. Having a third party present should help with negotiations... and could make all the difference if things get ugly.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: As I suspected, this chip Aventurine gave to you... is actually a miniature transmitter.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I don't know much about my life story... but I do have extraordinary skills!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What...? Hey, you can't just make up "titles" like that!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Heh, you're full of energy. Please send my regards to... the conductor, Pom-Pom. Please let them know that their friend has fond memories from his time aboard the Express, which he reminisces on every time he has a good drink.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Back here again...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beneath the sea surface of Memory Zone, in a garden closest to the full moon in the water, an elderly man rests on a recliner, enveloped in utter silence.
The Watchmaker, Mikhail Char Legwork, has passed into that endless, timeless dream, where no sound could ever awaken him.
Sometimes I feel like you're still alive, old friend, like you've still got so much to say and do.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: I've kept my promise... brought the future Trailblazers you've waited so long for. I don't know why you were so obsessed with that train, but I remember your last words...
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Don't let us down, old man.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Go ahead. His resting place... lies in the garden up ahead.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: As the words cease, Himeko nods ever so slightly in your direction. You take a deep breath, steady your mind, and turn your gaze towards the Watchmaker...

The dream bubble is clearly extraordinary. Perhaps the approach was wrong, you think, holding your breath and closing your eyes. With one knee on the ground, you press your forehead against the thin film coated in memoria.

Yet, before you, there remains an abyss of darkness. No crimson sun descending upon snow-capped mountains, no gentle laughter, no twinkling stars, no echoes of swords clashing, and most of all, no traces of "trailblaze"...
...There is nothing and nothing is there. Indubitably, this is but an empty dream bubble.
The first and last Nameless of Penacony...
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Mikhail Char Legwork, the Watchmaker.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Sure enough... the Watchmaker is the third Nameless. Even I could guess that one.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The legacy he left behind was a dream bubble. I believe inside that bubble, there's something that holds meaning only for the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: After all, when I checked its contents, I found nothing inside ... Maybe some Trailblaze runes? Even more enigmatic than me.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Well, let's have a look.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Wait, what's going on...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seriously... there's nothing inside this dream bubble?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: How could a dream bubble be empty?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph, just as I suspected.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: That old man always had this strange belief in the Nameless and the Trailblaze, and I never understood where he got that confidence from... especially since he never managed to get in touch with the Express while he was alive.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: I could never figure out what was going on in that old man's head, but this empty dream bubble is so typical of him. He was always full of weird fantasies... and incomprehensible romanticism.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: That mischievous old man... Well, I didn't expect him to leave anything concrete behind anyway.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Don't think that's the case, Gallagher. I'm sure Mikhail has left us the most precious thing of all.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Heh, don't start getting all philosophical on me, alright?
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: You press your hands against the dream bubble and the thick viscous memoria converges under strain, then stretches outward from your fingertips. As if weaving a delicate web, it gently cradles your palm.
A chill travels from your fingertips, carrying with it a myriad of vibrant and intertwined memories, as experience would suggest...
But this time, you see nothing at all.

Just as Mikhail believes in the Nameless of the future, we unconditionally believe in the Nameless of the past. How could they leave with regrets for the future when they were ready to dedicate their lives to the land they loved?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: There must be something contained in this dream bubble. It's just we haven't figured it out yet. You also have faith in the Watchmaker, don't you, Gallagher?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Well, I'm a follower of the Enigmata. My philosophy forbids me to have faith in anything.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: ...That's why I understand what "faith" means in the Path of Trailblaze, and I also want to know what he left behind. Heh, I'll leave it to you guys then.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Can I borrow your {RUBY_B#"Dormancy"}pet{RUBY_E#}? I need to make a trip back to Golden Hour and check something at the Dreamscape Sales Store...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's for Mikhail, and for the future of Penacony.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Brother...!
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...There's no need for words. You're safe, and that's all that matters.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Welcome to the Reverie Hotel. How may I help you?
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Greetings. We're the Nameless from the Astral Express, and we'd like to check in.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Astral Express? But I thought...
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Yes, my companions already checked in. My name is Dan Heng, and I believe my personal information is recorded in your system.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I see, but your companions said you wouldn't be coming due to a change of plans.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Hah! Now the plans have changed again!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: 10 system hours until Charmony Festival - The Reverie Hotel (Reality)
And you are...?
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Me? I'm Pom-Pom, a new Nameless who's also with the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: ...He's my fellow Trailblazer. We responded to The Family's invitation before he boarded the Express, so he wasn't registered in your system. Is it possible to accommodate him as well?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh, I see! Another one of the Nameless had a similar situation. Seems like a lot of people are joining the Trailblaze these days.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Since there is a precedent, it shouldn't be a problem. Just give me a second to contact your companions...
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: ...I'm sorry, dear guests, but it seems I'm unable to reach the other members of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: What do you mean by "unable to reach" them?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: My apologies. This is the first time I've encountered a situation like this. However, the system indicates that those guests are still in the Dreamscape.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: ...How about this? Give me their room number, and we'll go check on them ourselves.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I'm afraid that's not possible. I need to verify both of your identities before I can share any guest information.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: How about you just wake up someone? Let's say... Welt?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I'm sorry, but there are strict rules regarding forced awakening — it cannot be done without the proper clearance.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: So nothing works, huh? What's your solution then? Are you saying we sleep here, at the reception?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Please be patient. We need to contact your companions in order to confirm your identities...
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: And now it seems you need to confirm our identities before you can contact our companions.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It seems so.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: Fudge! Look, nothin' personal, but if you can't handle this, go find someone else who can, okay?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Please calm down, dear guests! I do recall that Mr. Sunday, the Oak Family Head, personally handled this issue earlier. Please wait a moment while I contact him.
rows.speaker: Alley

rows.text: I don't think she's trying to give us a hard time. She really just doesn't know what to do.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I have a bad feeling about this. You tried to contact them on the Express earlier, but they didn't respond.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Something doesn't seem right. I need to leave for a moment. You can stay here with the receptionist.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Sure thing — just don't keep me waiting forever.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: (Dan Heng seems pretty worried about his companions. I should give him some space. Stressing out about it won't help anything.)
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: (This place is too big... I better not wander too far in case he can't find me later.)
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Surely there'll be a lot of celebrities at the Charmony Festival. It's a great opportunity to make some valuable connections.
rows.speaker: Sabrina

rows.text: Don't enter the dream with such a utilitarian agenda!
rows.speaker: Jno

rows.text: Back already?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Hasn't she returned yet?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Nope. I'm starting to wonder if sending her to contact Sunday was a good idea.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Neither the staff nor the guests seem to know anything about what's happening in the Dreamscape, and wherever we go, all we see is people enjoying themselves... Definitely not a good sign.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I agree. Another unusual thing is that the Oak Family is supposed to be in charge of organizing the council and managing everything inside and outside the Dreamscape. However...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I walked around the hotel but didn't meet a single member of the Oak Family on such an important day.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well I'll be forked... if I remember correctly, the head of the Oak Family is that Sunday guy, right?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: We shouldn't linger here too long. Let's go back to the Express for now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not so fast. Have you ever robbed the IPC, bro? If you run away now, everyone will be chasing after you.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Are you suggesting we sit here and do nothing?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I wouldn't say "do nothing," but let's stay put for now. Even if The Family has ulterior motives, they couldn't have anticipated us showing up here. We're the surprise factor for them.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: They don't want to attract unwanted attention from certain outsiders, so they won't do anything reckless... See? The IPC lackeys are keeping a close eye on this hotel.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: ...If I were a Family member, I'd find an official excuse and keep the surprise factors here. If we just wait here, that would be like walking into their trap.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Of course, we don't need to walk into their trap. I gave a backup plan to the Memokeeper. If it turns out we won't be allowed to enter the Dreamscape, she'll order a drink for me in the VIP Lounge at the hotel in reality.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: A secret signal?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's right.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: A concrete object can indeed help the Memokeeper establish a connection with you... but Boothill, if you have more back-up plans in the future, I hope you'll let me know in advance.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm sorry, but it's one of my quirks. I have too many unreliable friends, and if I reveal that I have backup plans, things can... things can go awry. And that would leave all backup plans completely useless.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: How do we get into the VIP lounge?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This is where my street smarts come into play.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Wow! This bar is something else — certainly worthy of the Planet of Festivities.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Good evening, gentlemen.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: Hey... I have an order for a bottle of Asdana's White Oak. Can you help us find it?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Asdana's White Oak? I think there might be a misunderstanding. We don't serve that here.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: No way. Are you sure you're not mistaken?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: If someone had reserved such a beverage, I would definitely remember it. It sells for hundreds of thousands of credits per bottle, after all... I couldn't afford to cover for such an item if it were broken or lost.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: That's strange... could it be that the Memokeeper couldn't afford it?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Then what should we do now?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No need to rush. Let's grab some drinks first. Maybe I arrived too early and she hasn't come yet.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Let's see what kind of juice malts you all have here... Well, give me a glass of Hinnom Valley 40 Years. I'll have it neat, no ice.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Well, that's the most expensive one on the list. You have a taste for the finer things.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: Hah, it's on the house anyway...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: What can I get for you?
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: Anything you recommend is fine.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Then I would recommend today's special, Glass Village — it's Classic SoulGlad mixed with Leboom juice. It's refreshing and suits your cool demeanor. Just one minute.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: Ahh! This flavor... Dynamite Barbecue with Rocket Fuel... It really hits the spot! Truly the finest sherry cask-aged malt juice in the cosmos.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: "Dynamite Barbecue with Rocket Fuel"... Is that really something that humans enjoy?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey, this guy doesn't know anything at all.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: As long as you are satisfied, dear guests. Please enjoy.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: Let's give the Memokeeper another half system hour. If she doesn't show up, we'll need to come up with a new plan. In the meantime, let's take stock of the situation. What do you think?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: The situation is unclear. Something must have happened on the Planet of Festivities, but the public is unaware of it. Someone in a position of power within The Family must be covering it up.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's unusual for the followers of the Harmony to invite other factions, let alone the IPC and the Masked Fools... If what you said about the Emanator of the Nihility is true, the situation in Penacony is... a little complicated, to say the least.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Actually, there's something else I'm concerned about — regarding Acheron.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: As you know, the faction that follows the Path of The Hunt are some of the most dangerous folks in the Cosmos to mess with. I mean, who in their right mind would impersonate the Xianzhou Alliance or the Galaxy Rangers? It's like asking for a death wish...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Isn't there a saying among the Xianzhou people that "the Reignbow sect lets their Lux Arrow do all the beating..."
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Talking. Do all the talking.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well, you know what I mean. Even though the Galaxy Rangers have been out of sight for years, we've been keeping an eye on this region. Even the dumbest criminals know better than to mess with the Annihilation Gang, much less the Rangers.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: But that Acheron lady... she doesn't seem like a lunatic at all. On the contrary, she's highly logical and organized. She knows exactly when to hold back and when to strike without mercy.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: And you believe that someone like her would have an ulterior motive for impersonating a Galaxy Ranger?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm not entirely sure, but I do have my suspicions. Maybe she knows a Galaxy Ranger, or perhaps she's trying to lure us out for some reason... which I can't figure out.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Anyway, what worries me more are the anomalies within The Family. They've summoned followers from various paths for the festival. No matter how generous The Family might be, this move seems highly unusual.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Unless the invitations weren't sent by them. If that's the case, it's even more intriguing that The Family insists on organizing the Charmony Festival... despite the chaos.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Maybe it's Xipe the Harmony pulling the strings. You find it beyond human understanding because it wasn't arranged by humans at all.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: People do stupid things out of irrational impulses. They abandon their principles when self-interest is involved. They believe in things they know they shouldn't, and fudge— they even break their own rules!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: But Aeons don't. THEY stick to their determined path and never turn back, even if THEY reach a dead end!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: You think Xipe's will is behind all this?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It may not necessarily be Xipe, but there's definitely some higher entity involved. I know it may sound pessimistic, but if human free will were reliable, why would we even need Galaxy Rangers?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: It's much simpler when you boil it down to the Aeons and Paths, like how Lan always follows the Path of The Hunt or how the Express stays true to the Trailblaze despite Akivili's disappearance.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: But in my opinion, Akivili's fall holds significance for the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh? So you're saying the Nameless now have to take responsibility for their own choices because their "absolutely right" leader is gone?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Exactly. I believe the purpose of the journey isn't just about following a path that's always considered "absolutely right"...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's more about doing your best to choose the "right path" for yourself among countless possibilities, even with limited insight and judgment.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I don't know what you've been through, but I agree that people must take responsibility for their choices, because no one else can do it for them.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: That's why the Galaxy Rangers need to uncover the impostor... and figure out her true intentions.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Just in case, I have a backup plan if the Memokeeper doesn't show up... this is my final backup plan, I promise.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: You sure have a lot of cards up your sleeve.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well, going back to my old career would make things a lot easier.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: By the way, when you were walking around the hotel, did you happen to see any... important-looking guests?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: ...What's your plan?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's simple. We just grab some hostages and use them as bargaining chips with The Family. Or maybe we can even take their identities...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: No need for that. We'll return to the Express now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Wait! Are you getting scared? Draw your weapon! Let's make a big scene!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Are you leaving, esteemed guests? Would you like to cancel that Asdana's White Oak you just ordered?
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: ...Huh? Asdana's White Oak? But didn't you just say...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: Looks like you are a bit intoxicated, esteemed guests. You ordered a bottle of Asdana's White Oak just a moment ago.
rows.speaker: Anderson

rows.text: Looks like... your Memokeeper friend has finally arrived.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Oh, right! Sorry, my memory's not the best. You know, too many modifications and all. Anyway, let me check... Well fork me... It's Asdana's White Oak alright, and there's a note...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: ..."I'll be waiting for you on the Astral Express."
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: No mistake, that's her message to you. She knew the hotel wasn't safe, so she suggested we find another place.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well, looks like we took a detour, but now it's back to the Astral Express. So, what are we waiting for? Let's go!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: You're back? Two guests just boarded, saying they were looking for Boothill, so I told them to wait in the Parlor Car.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Oh! Just in time!
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: As he spoke, the old man's gaze remained fixed on the distance. Amidst the fine drizzle of black rain, countless shadowy hands emerged from the sea, shrouded in an ethereal mist, reaching out towards the sky one by one.
...Two guests?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: She's one of them. Look, we welcome all passengers on the Astral Express, but sneaking in like that... You have no regard for etiquette!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: My apologies, conductor. It was an oversight on my part. I assumed you were already acquainted with the Garden... Given the chaotic situation in Penacony, the Nameless are the only ones we can truly trust right now.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: You are the Memokeeper?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Pleased to meet you, Dan Heng. I've seen you in others' memories. And as for Boothill... This is our first face-to-face meeting. I hope you enjoyed that bottle of Asdana's White Oak. You sure have a refined taste.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Finally, Memokeeper! Well, let's cut to the chase. Spill everything you know.
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: That's precisely what I intend to do. But before that, please allow me to introduce myself. My name is Black Swan, and I serve the Garden of Recollection as a Memokeeper. As for Acheron's story...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I'm sure she knows it better than I do.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Greetings. I'm Acheron.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: What!? You Garden of Recollection shirtbag, you betrayed me!?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: I apologize, but she did that at my request. Due to certain... reasons, I have been exiled by The Family. Thankfully, this Memokeeper came to my aid and helped me escape their surveillance unnoticed.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: To be honest, it was more like stalking than helping, and the process was far from "unnoticed"... But we did escape.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I asked her to guide me to a place beyond The Family's reach and to contact a few trustworthy individuals, namely all of you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Trustworthy? Ha... hahahahaha! Son of a nice lady! You think I'm dumb or something?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: How about this? I'll put a few bullet holes in your head and see what secrets spill out, then we can talk about "trust"...
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: It doesn't have to be like that. I'm willing to answer all your questions, but not right now... If my cover hadn't been blown, we might have had more time, but at the moment, we don't have any other options.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: No other options? What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Boothill

rows.text: This is the only way I can ensure everyone's safety...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I kindly request an immediate warp jump out of the Asdana star system.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: This passenger is requesting...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: As far as I can tell, she's not a threat and seems to be telling the truth.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I've briefly traveled with your companions and know their whereabouts, Dan Heng. Please rest assured, your Nameless companions are safe, but they need our help.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: As for Boothill, as you may have guessed... I've been waiting for you. Galaxy Rangers are known for their elusive nature and limited contact with each other, so this is the only way I could "reach out" to you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Only by doing this can I find a true Galaxy Ranger and fulfill a long-standing promise...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...To return "his" relics to their rightful owner.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Someone once told me... that every rainfall is like a gift from the heavens, a sign of their mercy upon the world.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Raindrops are said to be the tears of the Gods, shed in response to the sorrows of the world. Their constant pouring is a reminder that the Gods haven't abandoned us yet.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: So...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: How long has this rain been going on for?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: I used to believe, just like you, that it would eventually stop. Years and decades passed... and in the end, such hope faded away before the rain did.
Looks like the God you mentioned doesn't exist after all.
Well, let me share a story with you...
Mortals who walk the Paths are like sailors on a vast ocean, leaving behind a trail that creates countless ripples of possibilities. These ripples last longer than the fleeting lifetimes of humans.
And for some, their presence leaves such a strong mark that it's reflected in the waves.
Like... those shadows on the ocean.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Sin Thirsters... the obsessions of the Pathstriders. They emerge from the depths of IX, seeing themselves as masters of their own destiny, unknowingly repeating the actions of their past lives.
They emerge from the Nihility and head toward it, leading purposeless lives. However, these hollow phantoms...
...They were once my dear companions, a group of Galaxy Rangers.
Are you watching over them?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Watching over them? No, I'm guiding them toward transcendence.

It was a brutal war, a crusade that shook the universe. The universe witnessed the fall of Zulo the Lord Ravager, but it came at a price... A price so hefty that only those who were there still remember.

The unwavering determination of The Hunt followers persists even in death, so someone must guide these lost souls to their life beyond. They were heroes in their time, and they shouldn't be reduced to mere puppets of the Nihility.
As for me... I've suffered too many losses on that battlefield to advance any further, and that makes me the most fitting person to carry out this task.
But you know, these Sin Thirsters... They are not who they used to be.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: Does this seem pointless to you?
Well, some tasks have to be done, even if they are pointless.
I can help you.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: For what?
For the meaning of the Nihility... that's what I've been seeking.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: ...I see. After all, this realm is off-limits to ordinary souls, right?
Thank you, stranger. I wish that you find what you seek.
Before we part ways, I have one more question...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: It is true that their actions and even their entire lives may seem pointless from our perspective, but if, and it's just an "if"...
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: If this is what the departed ones expected, should we try to change it?
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: A good question, and a profound one... I don't know the answer.
What I do know is that one day, I too will pass away. I hope that when that day comes...
Someone will stand at my grave and place a bouquet of flowers.
"When I appeared as a child, my speech, mindset, and soul reflected immaturity and innocence."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "As I grew into adulthood, I left behind my childlike side."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I humbly request your blessings, esteemed advocate of Xipe.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: Come to me, my Kinship. I have sought THEIR presence with us.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: 9 system hours until Charmony Festival - Golden Hour
As you wish.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: I have faithfully served the Alfalfa Family for nearly a decade, promoting the Path of the Harmony to the best of my ability. However, I made a mistake yesterday. While I was preparing dinner for The Family Head, I accidentally dropped a prepared dish on the floor.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: Out of laziness, I lied and claimed that everything was ready. Although the Head has dismissed me as punishment, it has been tough to sleep with the guilt still gnawing at me, as I worried that the seeds of evilness may have taken root in my soul. So, I confess to you now to seek atonement for my sins.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: Do you sincerely repent and vow to change your ways?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Have you examined your soul and confessed all your sins?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Are you willing to accept the process of atonement?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Very well. Show your dedication and goodwill to The Family, and you shall be reinstated among them. Now, please leave in peace.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Praise Xipe. And thank you, esteemed advocate.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: I... I wholeheartedly confess to you... Please, pardon my sins!
rows.speaker: Panicked Dreamchaser

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: Rest assured. I have implored THEIR presence to be with us. As long as you are sincere, absolution will be granted.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Yes.
rows.speaker: Halovian Servant

rows.text: Oh! Oh, great... you know, I... I arrived in Penacony as a stowaway. I sold everything to get a ticket... my house, my land... and... my two children...
rows.speaker: Panicked Dreamchaser

rows.text: I see... Please go on.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Next. Please step forward.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My children were starving, and I hoped they'd have a chance at survival if they became slaves here. If... if I can strike it rich here, I'll lift them out of that situation... and give them the life they deserve...
rows.speaker: Panicked Dreamchaser

rows.text: But, but, the Bloodhound Family got wind of it. They're on my tail... hunting me down... I thought I could bring my kids here! It was all my fault... all my fault...
rows.speaker: Panicked Dreamchaser

rows.text: The Family is ready to forgive all sinners. I'll ask the Bloodhound Family to cease their pursuit. You don't need to live in fear anymore.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Thank you, thank you! I'll work my hardest to redeem my children and make them part of The Family... P—Praise the Harmony!
rows.speaker: Panicked Dreamchaser
