rows.text: Hey, long time no see, Mr. Sunday! The most esteemed individual in Penacony and... the next leader of the Oak Family, right?
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: ...I have sought THEIR presence with us. Let us proceed.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Sure, let's just get this over with. Ahem! I have sinned. Please forgive me! I wasted half a pizza at breakfast... and a bottle of SoulGlad.
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: That's it. Nothing more. Can we wrap this up? I've got a Roboball game to catch, you know?
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: ...Next. Please step forward.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Do you... seek to atone for your sins through good deeds?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My "sins"!? Starting to sound like a saint, eh? Let me tell you something — Neither The Family nor you have the right to judge me.
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: You think nobody knows what your precious Family has done? About the Watchmaker, huh? Don't kid yourself, feather-brain. Those Dreamchasers might be fooled by your act, but don't fool yourself.
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: Before you start spouting off your holy verses, answer me this... Where does the power of the Oak Family come from? And your power? What makes you think you can sit there, all high and mighty, looking down on everyone else?
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: Well, I've spent enough time in confession today to enter the Harmony's paradise, right? Then I'll take my leave. Good luck with your election, and... don't make me regret my investments in you.
rows.speaker: Pepeshi Merchant

rows.text: O, revered Triple-Faced Soul, hear my doubts...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Who can judge the strong when their power hides their crimes?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Who can vouch for the weak when they will pay any price to survive?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Who can comfort the purest souls when even they get led astray?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: If "the strong defending the weak" is truly the foundation of paradise...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...then who— who is responsible for the suffering and anguish in this wretched world?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Brother... Brother...?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...Brother? Are you alright?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...I'm fine. I've been working long hours, and I just made a trip to Dreamflux Reef and back... So I'm a bit out of sorts. But it'll all be over before we know it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You've been working non-stop on the Charmony Festival, Mr. Sunday, and no one could have predicted this incident. Even if the Stellaron does pose a grave threat, I still feel sorry for all the trouble we've caused you.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hehe, no need to worry about troubling anyone. The Charmony Festival was meant to spread joy and harmony across the Cosmos. But now that we know the truth, I'm afraid we'll have to cancel it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It has always been our wish to make everyone happy, so... we'll do our best to explain everything to the Dreammaster. I'm sure he'll understand.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Even if the negotiation does not go smoothly... I'll refuse to go on stage. Without the Chordmaster, the {RUBY_B#Embodiment of Harmony}Harmonious Choir{RUBY_E#} would not arrive, and the Charmony Festival would be just a grand performance, and nothing more.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I'm relieved to see your determination.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Y'know, since arriving in Penacony, we haven't had any contact with this Dreammaster himself. I'd heard of the heads of the five major lineages, but the Dreammaster is a mystery to me.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Dreammaster rarely grants an audience — even for us. But given the urgency of the situation, he's agreed to meet us in person.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Perhaps you'll be the first guest to meet the Dreammaster in years, Mr. Yang.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Let's hope we can reach a consensus that satisfies everyone.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Indeed — let us hope so.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's about time. We'll have to get ready for the meeting... I apologize for any inconvenience caused by the urgency.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Don't worry. I'll be waiting here.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh, dear... it's Mr. Sunday! Hey, come over here! Hahaha...
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: Looks like someone needs help... let's go check it out.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Oh, Mr. Sunday... Hey there! Okay, see the moon in the sky? It's about the size of the cap on my SoulGlad bottle!
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: If I just reached out my hand... I could grab the moon, couldn't I?
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: The moon... You mean the Grand Theater?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Oh, yeah! Haha, look at me! I've been away from home for too long... I must be missing that moon... *hiccup*
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: But... it's no big deal! The Grand Theater here looks much better than the moon back home... It's just... magnificent!
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: They told me not to sell everything I had just to come to Penacony... Tsk, how short-sighted!
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: Selling everything you had? Why would you go to such lengths?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Why? Can't you see...? Life back home is miserable... It's not really living at all.
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: It's better to be here in Penacony! No pain, no worries about tomorrow, just sweet dreams! You can do whatever you want! That's what I call living... *hiccup* Yeah, now this is the life!
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: Is this... truly "living"...?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: *hiccup* Huh...? What did you just say, young lady...? I didn't quite catch that...
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: Oh, it's nothing, sir. You see, the traffic on Glaux Avenue can be dangerous. How about I ask a Bloodhound Family member to escort you to Aideen Park over there so you can continue enjoying your sweet dream?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Oh... yeah, that's a great idea! Wow, no wonder you're the leader of this sweet dream! You're totally a lifesaver!
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: See you around, Mr. Sunday! And... It was nice chatting with you... *hiccup*
rows.speaker: Drunken Guest

rows.text: What's up, sister?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This is the land of the dreams, but why do they live like this?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The man we ran into... he doesn't seem happy at all.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: The Stellaron issue concerns the life and death of everyone on Penacony. If anyone has a better suggestion, the Crew is more than willing to listen. Also, it'd be best to tell us the ins and outs of that meeting—
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...This way, we'll at least know what Welt and Miss Robin are dealing with, and the reason why they failed to make our appointment.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Competitors, allow me to introduce the rules of this challenge to you.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Ah, Navigator, that is precisely my intention. With all present, let's begin by discussing the details of that meeting.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Let's talk about our tribulations and choices, our ideals and beliefs...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And our final course of action, the only path to take.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...You mean to say, that for the longest time, there have been scoundrels who would use the Charmony Festival that I have bequeathed to the masses... as a tool to realize their ambition?
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Indeed, Dreammaster. Once the Charmony Festival begins, the Stellaron's powers, along with the song will be broadcast across the entire planet of Penacony... And then, everyone in their dreams will be unable to awaken.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hmm, this is indeed surprising to me. The Dreamscape is maintained by the collective effort of the Five Families. If someone were to use the Charmony Festival to recklessly disseminate the power of the Stellaron, this individual must hold a position of great authority...
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Do you have any suspects?
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: I'd like to ask: Did you really not know of the Stellaron's existence?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Heh... I would've never thought that this Nameless would point the spear at me, quite astonishing indeed.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: If I have offended, the Astral Express extends its sincere apologies... but the current circumstances are dire, and leave no room for meticulous inquiry. We're doing this out of concern for the Dreamscape's safety... so if you could, please alleviate our concerns.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Dreammaster, it's just to prove that the Charmony Festival has nothing to do with the Stellaron. If we're being overly cautious... I will return to the stage to offer tribute in song, just per the arrangement.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Sunday, Robin, I've watched you two grow up, and know your dispositions like the back of my hand. Both of you right now, can surely be lauded as {RUBY_B#Harmony}THEIR{RUBY_E#} most devout advocates... I already know your resolve.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: The magnitude of this matter is enormous, and cannot be taken lightly. Since Mr. Yang has asked with such earnestness, I will personally respond in kind. If there is a need, the entire Oak Family will be mobilized to heed your call.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Sunday, might I ask you to beseech THEM to cast THEIR light unto me, and question me in THEIR stead, so that no lies may be concealed?
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: I will do as you command.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Robin, could I entrust you to be present as a witness, to document the truth, and to proclaim my innocence, so that all slander may be utterly dispelled?
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: I will do as you command.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: May thy will be carried out on earth... just as it is in the heavens.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "Oh, Triple-Faced Soul, please sear his tongue and palms with a hot iron, so that he will not be able to fabricate lies and make false vows."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Let us begin. There is nothing else to prepare.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Understood.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Question: Have you devoted your life to your God, never worshiping other Gods?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Do you love your God as you do yourself, always heeding THEIR admonishments?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Have you strayed from the path expected by your God, betraying THEIR name?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Have you ever been inordinate with your asks of your God, coveting more than the foundation of the creation itself?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then, a final question...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Do you swear to fulfill all vows, past, present and future?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: With the Aeon as my witness, if I do not deliver on my words, or if I renege on my vows, may I be cursed in accordance with divine law.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: ...THEY have seen your faith, and have endorsed your faith. With this, it can be evidenced—
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Just a moment.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Beautiful! Beautiful! Truly a captivating contest! It is through you that I realize, to uphold the honor of Idrila, I must further hone my skills... What a beautiful lesson indeed!
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: Go forth, my dear friend, beautiful miss, the audition's crown is yours to claim...
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: I shall remain here, gazing from afar as you bask in the limelight, joining the audience in offering you the most heartfelt cheers and applause.
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: We don't have much time... May fate allow us to meet again, Knight of Beauty.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What is it, Mr. Yang?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Beautiful! Beautiful! Truly a captivating contest! It is through you that I realize, to uphold the honor of Idrila, I must further hone my skills... What a beautiful lesson indeed!
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: Go forth, my dear friend, beautiful miss, the audition's crown is yours to claim...
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: I shall remain here, gazing from afar as you bask in the limelight, joining the audience in offering you the most heartfelt cheers and applause.
rows.speaker: Argenti

rows.text: We don't have much time... May fate allow us to meet again, Knight of Beauty.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...I have another question I hope to have answered.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: To my understanding, The Family's harmony and prosperity have never relied on so-called "divine laws"...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The "God" you both mentioned... are THEY truly {RUBY_B#The Harmony}Xipe{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Yang should know that those belonging to The Family toil together as if they were kin, embracing solidarity and unity under THEIR Light. All duplicity is laid bare before the Harmony.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Such a delicate and complex symphony, which other God could perfectly harmonize this if not for the Great One, Xipe?
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "Perfectly harmonize"... Therein lies the problem. It isn't an outsider lurking in the shadows who changed the Harmony, but a dissonance that has surreptitiously emerged from within this very symphony itself.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: In the distant past, there existed an Aeon. With one flick of the wrist, THEY crafted the laws of the cosmos. THEIR followers formed the Beyond-the-Sky Choir, spreading solemn and reverent hymns throughout the universe.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Later, THEY fell. The route traversed by this Aeon clashed with the Harmony, ultimately being absorbed and fused into it. The chorus that once reverberated across worlds fell silent, and when it echoed anew, it was transformed into the hymn of Harmony...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Though an Aeon may perish, paths with no masters still linger. In the all-forgiving Harmony... echoes of bygone dissonance may subtly arise.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Yang...
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Being overly astute can be a detriment, especially when you find yourself alone, and without allies.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: Hmph... so this is how it is.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: For the sake of our grand cause, Sunday, please afford these two an opportunity to rest.
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: What...?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Sorry, Robin, it's just you... I did not wish for you to know this. It's a pity that things have turned out this way.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So this is the true reason I can't sing? The shadow that envelops Penacony is actually...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: We were never children of the Harmony. Our ideal paradise... could not have been crafted by Xipe. True bliss can only be guaranteed by the "one" who transcends the many.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Within the foundation of law, humanity establishes civilization...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And through Harmony, we obtain Order.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Unbelievable, to think that there would be... remnants of the Order on Penacony.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What have you done with Mr. Yang and Miss Robin!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry. I just gave them some time alone to ponder their fates.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You should know that these actions make you an enemy of the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Should we need to stand against the Nameless, it would only be myself and the Oak family involved. But we haven't reached that point yet, have we?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Your efforts for the justice of Penacony are evident to everyone and have been widely observed.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Smart kid. You're just as sharp as the other one.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Patience is a virtue. However, I won't hold it against you. On the contrary, I'm here to make my intentions clear.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Oh I intend to, but that hinges on the outcome of this negotiation.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: If it is the Order that drove you to imprison Welt and Robin, and you're using them to coerce our compliance, then there'll be no point in entertaining any type of discussion.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You're mistaken, Miss Himeko. They are in very safe hands, and just as The Family has always proclaimed — no one can be harmed in the Dreamscape, least of all in the beautiful new world belonging to the Order.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Penacony and the entire universe have witnessed far too much innocent bloodshed. The strong wield their blades against the weak, and the victors push the vanquished to the brink of life...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Natural selection — the world abides by this principle, establishing the well-being of humanity atop the corpses of the downtrodden. Only {RUBY_B#Pathstriders of Order}we{RUBY_E#}, or rather I, possess the power to put an end to this farce.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So you've decided to resurrect a dead Aeon? No one's ever done such a thing.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If Miss Himeko is interested, let's draw back the veil and speak candidly. I've always firmly believed that people can understand one another through peaceful means.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm willing to divulge the unembellished truth as to the intentions of the Order's Pathstriders, so that you will make better judgment for the Astral Express, for Penacony, and for this stretch of the universe. Words can hardly do justice to the beauty of that ideal...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So come with me, everyone. Let us retrace our steps and see once again where this road leads.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Huh, where'd he go?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Welcome. This isn't any location in Penacony's Dreamscape. It's my inner world. The reason the scenery before you remains unchanged is because your consciousness has drawn on similar concepts to fill in the gaps.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That means...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... I'm not entirely sure, but... let's give it a try.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Wait, you managed to choose the right door on your first try?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did you do the same to Welt?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Tuning allows you to intuitively grasp my feelings, which also means that I cannot hide anything from you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now, everyone, please look at the huge screen. The road we once took begins here.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Look, there it is.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We're going to the opposite side, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, we should turn left here...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Huh? Something feels different about this place?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is it. I remember this corridor.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Up ahead is... Grandpa's study. It was in that room that I saw him the last time.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: This is it...!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: This is the Dream Jigsaw, right? So, we're supposed to find the exit? But where can we find the last piece...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do you remember, [Trailblazer]? You said you obtained a mysterious shard when you stumbled into this place.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: From this point on, you will witness the numerous decisions I've faced. I've selected a portion of these to share with you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hey, the shape seems to match. So, this shard is also connected to Misha?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like we're just one step from revealing the truth. Let's get to the other side and investigate.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You want to talk terms with us?
I believe after going through similar predicaments, you'll be able to better understand my thoughts.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Stop beating around the bush and get to the point.
Let's begin. The first decision: A story about a baby bird.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Give Mr. Yang back to us, now!
I can't decipher his intentions right now... but based solely on the question, I would probably choose to build that dove a cage...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Even if I was gonna release it back into the sky, it'd have to be strong enough to fly first. If I left it where I found it... I fear it'd never get the chance to fly ever again.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: You've imprisoned us?
Who in their right mind would expose their inner-self like this?
It looks like he really has no intention of imprisoning us. If it's just a quiz, I suppose it's fine to humor him.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Back to the question: I would personally choose to build the little Charmony Dove a cage.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Make the decision.
Think it over some more.
No special reason. I do think that a fledgling should have the right to fly in the sky... But if it can't even live to that point, then there's nothing to talk about to begin with.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Make the decision.
Think it over some more.
That guy just casually throws this kind of question at us? What exactly is his deal? But fine, I'll answer I guess...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Make the decision.
Think it over some more.
If it were me... I guess I'd choose to build a cage for the little Charmony Dove.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Make the decision.
Think it over some more.
After all, leaving it there, it's bound to get hurt by wild animals or something... And that'd just be too sad.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Make the decision.
Think it over some more.
Interesting. Since you've made up your mind, allow me to reveal what fate this choice will bring to the fledgling.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Exactly, this is where you and Firefly encountered "Death," which we now know as "Dormancy." Considering its connection to Dreamflux Reef, it's not surprising it appeared here.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hey, don't tease! I was just being a bit sentimental.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm not an elder. I was just being a bit sentimental.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Perhaps every adventurer far from home carries a fountain within their soul. Even though the other side of the sea remains shrouded in the unknown, the fountain in front of his house serves as a compass, leading him back to his cherished ones.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: March, do you remember when [Trailblazer] mentioned a "Clockie" that only {M#he}{F#she} could see?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A memetic life that can only be seen by a select few... It's just like a hidden message... left by someone for the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Of course. We've come this far. Surely there's no other option than moving forward.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Of course. We've come this far. Surely there's no other option than moving forward.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on... Stop joking at a moment like this. We've come this far. Surely there's no other option than moving forward.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Then let's proceed together to the end of this dream... and tell Mikhail our decision.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, you're right! We've even dealt with a Lord Ravager of the Destruction, so a follower of the Order won't be a big deal!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A—Are you backing out now!? We've even dealt with a Lord Ravager of the Destruction, so a follower of the Order won't be a big deal!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You...! Every time an important moment arrives, you hesitate.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Anyway, we can't leave the Stellaron unchecked. This is about trailblazing a bright future for Penacony and fulfilling Mikhail's and his predecessors' long-cherished wishes.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'm happy to see that you made a choice similar to ours. If your mind is made up, let me reveal the outcome of this choice.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This story happened when I was appointed as Bronze Melodia — a position exclusive to the Oak Family, charged with listening to the problems and vexations of Dreamscape residents, and providing them with the relevant guidance.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It was during that period that I had the opportunity to hear voices from all corners of the Dreamscape: Joy, sorrow, arrogance, regret... The complex tapestry of human nature that formed the world, and I was fortunate to catch a glimpse of it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: He was a Dreamchaser, and an illegal stowaway. Just like the rest of them, he came to Penacony in search of a better life, except that, to most people, the price he paid... I suppose you could say it was "everything."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: He told me "I sold everything I could at home." — the house, the land, even his two children... He said he could not afford to raise them, and that at least they could eat if they lived as slaves.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: He had a plan in place: He would buy back his children once he had made his fortune, and enjoy Penacony's beautiful dream with them. Alas, his plan to smuggle himself was somewhat clumsy — and he was sniffed out by those pigheaded Hounds.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: After hearing the Dreamchaser's story, I immediately appealed to the Bloodhound Family to cease their pursuit. That way, at least he could live peacefully. But I was still too naive to the ways of the world — I did not anticipate that what I thought was a kind gesture would later lead to dire consequences...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'll tell you the outcome soon. For now, I'd like you all to make a choice—
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Will you do as I did, and try to convince the Bloodhound Family to stop their pursuit, so that the Dreamchaser may live peacefully and realize his wishes?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Or will you remain silent, leaving him to languish while the Hounds are hot on his heels, until his inevitable judgment arrives?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I look forward to everyone's decisions. Who knows, perhaps they might even alter the outcome of this tragedy.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: A Dreamchaser story... If I acted out of kindness, I would probably ask the Bloodhounds to stop their pursuit and lend him a hand.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But, what cruel repercussion would this choice result in? I think, Sunday must have been deeply impressed by the limitations of "the strong defending the weak" through this incident.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It seems illegal stowaways are really quite common on Penacony... But that guy in the story, I don't think he deserves any sympathy at all.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He sold his kids to chase a dream... Even if he intended to go back for them, it's still insanely irresponsible.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's a "tuning" process, stronger in effect and more draining on the mind. [Trailblazer] has experienced it before, so {M#he}{F#she} should understand what it entails.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: With that thought, there is only one choice: Let the Bloodhounds send him back home! This person deserves to be punished!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This question... surely it has some connection to the baby bird story — and this connection is precisely the breakthrough Sunday aims to use to persuade us...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...I'd probably choose to ask the Bloodhounds to cease their pursuit.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It seems you, like me, are pondering whether a different choice could have led to a better outcome. Sadly, his fate would only be more tragic.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm honored to witness you arriving at the same decision. Out of respect, I'll share with you the dire consequences that my choice back then brought about.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This story happened the day I was appointed the Oak Family Head. At that time, Mr. Gopher Wood was the current Dreammaster, and as per his wish, we had a private conversation.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What surprised me was that the Dreammaster had only come to deliver a letter to me. He let me read its contents. It was a letter... from my sister.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The letter contained the usual pleasantries, anecdotes from her travels — nothing out of the ordinary. Just as I started wondering how this letter related to our discussion, the Dreammaster began to speak.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Do you know who wrote this letter?"
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "My sister, of course. But why would you personally visit me to hand me a letter from my sister containing mere trivialities?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "To help you grasp the full scope of this issue. Do you know where Robin is at this moment?"
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "From what the letter indicates... She must be in Kasbelina-VIII, correct? She's touring there right now..."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Correct. Has she mentioned anything about a stray bullet?"
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "A stray bullet? What..."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "A war has broken out on that planet. It is because of this very reason that Robin chose this destination... To spread the word of the Harmony, and to save the lives of that planet, she personally made for the frontlines."
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "She hoped to ease the people's suffering with song, and was willing to brave mortal danger to deliver the IPC's medical supplies... Unfortunately, stray bullets show no such compassion."
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "Is she alright!?"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "If the operation was successful, she should probably be recovering in the field hospital."
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "By the Aeon above, the bullet struck her neck directly... Yet, possibly as a reward for her consistent deeds of Harmony, it didn't hit any vital arteries. Once you've attended to your outstanding tasks, it'd be advisable to write her back as soon as possible."
rows.speaker: "Dreammaster"

rows.text: "Those... damned savages! I'll pack my bags right away... My gratitude for bringing this to my attention, Mr. Gopher Wood!"
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now, you understand why she always wears such elaborate neck ornaments, don't you?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: How could this happen... Miss Robin...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's all in the past, so please don't worry. I share this in the meager hope that you will understand the Harmony's limitations and predicament. As grandiose as "the strong defending the weak" sounds, many times, it is nothing more than wishful thinking.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Likewise, I've prepared one last question, one last choice. But rest assured, this choice will not have any grave consequences.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Because this is merely a figment of imagination, a nightmare that has haunted me through countless nights. If you ever had the opportunity to make a choice like I did...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Would you still support Robin's journey on the Path of Harmony?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I often feel like I've dreamt of similar scenes on certain nights. In the dream, I see blurry faces. I don't know who they are, but I sympathize with all of them, fighting for survival against some unfathomable force...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Their confusion and fear are lucid to me... But I also remember they chose never to give up — just like Miss Robin.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer], if Mr. Sunday's question leaves you puzzled, you should find the answer from your own experiences.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: With each Trailblaze, dangers and tribulations will surely follow, but would you ever back away? Would you stop March and Dan Heng from reaching their next destination? I believe you have an answer of your own in your heart.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Miss Robin's courage is admirable. And here I was, thinking she was just another superstar celebrity...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But the fact that she's also Mr. Sunday's younger sister... No, I doubt he'd wish harm on his own flesh and blood, no matter how grand the ambition.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Heh... I see.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I am now aware of everyone's stances.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Raising these questions merely serves to illustrate one point: The plight of Penacony cannot be salvaged by the Harmony. The true foundation for a Sweetdream Paradise can only be established through the Order where the strong govern the weak.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I know the suffering of being tormented, the turmoil of losing your way, how sorrow... and even despair, set in when matters don't work out. All of this causes me unending pain, because this is not what "happiness" is at all.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: We must teach the weak how to live a happy life. And this life isn't some noble propriety that the upper crust preaches, but in definitive terms, a way of survival that belongs to everyone.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So, what is your definition of living a happy life?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Good question. Human consciousness is fundamentally an illusion, a cage known as "self-worth." People lured in by this illusion, make mistakes, yet still ask that external influences bear the burden.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When one mistake after the next permeates the masses, they become impossible to trace... Thus, the amassing of these individual cages culminate to form a prison, a place dictated only by the rule of "survival of the fittest."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Nature is always accompanied by predation and sacrifice... Its antithesis is known as Order.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That is what I want to do: Unite people's happiness under the banner of Order. They won't need to make bitter choices any longer, nor face the weaknesses of humanity. They can cast aside their primal instincts, to build a haven for mankind.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Simply describing thoughts is far too abstract, so allow me to provide a simple example: As you all may know, there are societal norms like "weekends" and "long weekends" that exist on some worlds.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: During these hard-earned rest days, people are given the chance to extricate themselves from the stresses of everyday life, allowing a certain tranquility to return to their souls.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And it is only on these days, that people do not have to adhere to the law where the strong prey on the weak — they can live out their lives happily during these brief intermissions. It's just a pity... that two or three days are still too fleeting compared to the span of a lifetime.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: From where I stand, society's ideal system should be "seven rest days." Following Sunday, there should ensue a second, a third, and indeed an infinite procession of Sundays. This should be the face of the new world — idyllic, eternal, peaceful days.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And thus, every person can return to their base selves in this utopia. Some gaze in reverence at the stars, pouring their whole beings into calculating the distance between us and the isolated world of {RUBY_B#Silver Rail's starting point}Pegana{RUBY_E#}. Meanwhile, some seek refuge in quiet corners, holding one another, unencumbered by the chains of unwelcome obligations...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: There would be no need to bear the hardships of reality. Only in this way can humanity face the inevitable end with the purest of spirit. Living a life of dignity — this is what it is to live in bliss.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Miss Firefly, you who are stricken with Entropy Loss Syndrome — you of all would surely understand this?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It sounds... like a flawless theory...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But... what is the price to attain all this?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The cost is minute, merely a personal... and eternal sacrifice. If this paradise is to be maintained for everyone, someone must remain trapped in solitary wakening, until the end of the cosmos.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Wakening... Which means that this so-called paradise is still a dream. Stepping into this paradise means forsaking reality, correct?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It is not forsaking, but transcending. Flesh, blood, sorrow, weakness. If the physical is the root of spiritual suffering, it is only logical that we defeat it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But in this supposed "bliss," people won't have defeated their demons. The chance to overcome their tribulations would be forever lost to them. In other words... it is an escape.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's another way of understanding it, but there is no shame in escape. On the contrary, the seeds of escape exist in everyone's hearts.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't you agree, Miss Firefly? And as for why life slumbers? It is because we are afraid to awaken from our dreams.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But this is not in conflict with the grand plan. Only in acknowledging this, can we truly understand the frailty of human nature, and from there, show compassion and protection.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I... I admit that you are a born leader. Your perspective on humanity brims with pessimism, yet you express compassion for all, even when your heart pities them.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: But unlike you — I live for the "self." From my perspective, individuals making choices for themselves is their birthright.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The want to escape may be innate in the weak, but whether they are weak or not... It is not up to another to decide.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Perhaps in your mind, you also view me as "weak"?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Because I don't think so.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Since Miss Firefly has said her piece, the Astral Express will also naturally give you our answer.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We'll leave it to you, [Trailblazer]. Just as Mr. Mikhail instructed before: Tell him our choice...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What is this place...?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Does this place ring any bells, Misha?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I... don't know, but I feel a sense of déjà vu. What is this place?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: It's the realm within a dream bubble. This was left to the Astral Express by a Nameless, but weirdly when we entered it, it was completely empty.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Dr. Edward from the Dreamscape Sales Store told me that dreams are formed from memories, and a dream bubble can't take shape if its core is empty.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So I thought you might be able to help us in unraveling this mystery, Misha? As a hotel {RUBY_B#bellboy}doorman{RUBY_E#}, you know Penacony best among us.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hmm, I don't know much about dream bubbles, but if you want to figure out what this mansion is... I'll do my best!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I'm counting on you then.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko... I still don't get it. Why were you so sure that Misha had a connection with this dream bubble?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wasn't sure. It was just a hunch, but since Misha feels familiar with this place... my hunch might be correct.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Exactly, this is where you and Firefly encountered "Death," which we now know as "Dormancy." Considering its connection to Dreamflux Reef, it's not surprising it appeared here.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The question now is — Who brought you here? Based on the clues we have so far, it's unlikely to be that Masked Fool, so identifying them is crucial to us.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We're drawing closer to the truth once more. Let's give Misha some time, as I believe he'll unveil the secret of this dream bubble.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Alright, but there are doors all over the place... Which one should we choose...? Do you have any idea, Misha?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm... I guess... maybe this way?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: (Check the inventory.)
I... I'm not entirely sure, but... let's give it a try.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Wait, you managed to choose the right door on your first try?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This place looks a bit familiar...
Weird, this place is quite different from the hotel, but I just... I feel like I've been here before and... even lived here for a while.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: This place feels a bit nostalgic...
Don't sigh, or you'll start getting gray hair...
If I remember correctly, there should be a fireplace down that hallway. Clockie and I used to sit by the fire, listening to the crackling of firewood.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: You're talking like an elder.
And... And the room on the other side was... the toy room. I loved spreading out all the toys from the box on the floor and making up stories for each of them.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Hold on, this doesn't make sense. Didn't I grow up in Dreamflux Reef? So, what is this place...?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Yeah, you're the only one still in the dark.
March, do you remember when [Trailblazer] mentioned a "Clockie" that only {M#he}{F#she} could see?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Too bad I don't know either...
Yeah, I noticed that, too.

This could be a case of amnesia. But don't worry, Misha, it's common for everyone to forget certain aspects of the past. Those memories haven't vanished. They're just lying in the depths of your mind. We can surely get them back.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Wait, really?
I'll choose the Trailblaze.
Of course. We've come this far. Surely there's no other option than moving forward.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I want to witness the legacy.
Of course. We've come this far. Surely there's no other option than moving forward.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I object!
Since this place seems familiar to you, why don't we explore a few more rooms and see if you can recall anything more?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, then let's check out the rooms I just mentioned.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Not long ago...
Mikhail, that's the name. Now we all know him as the Watchmaker.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: So, who is he talking to? Do you know anything about it, Misha?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm sorry, I don't know much about the Watchmaker, but Mikhail...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Anything special about that name?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Mikhail... is Grandpa's name.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Grandpa? Do you mean... you're the Watchmaker's grandson?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But we haven't heard anything about the Watchmaker having descendants, and the name "Mikhail" is not rare. Perhaps it's merely a coincidence.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Could you tell us more about your grandpa Mikhail?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, sure. He was a seafarer who fearlessly ventured into mysterious seas and storms. He was always on the sea and had a lot of friends who accompanied him on his travels.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Every time he came back, he'd share his logbook with me and tell me about his adventures at sea. I want to become a great adventurer just like him.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: It appears that the seafarer has nothing to do with the Watchmaker. So, perhaps it's just a coincidence?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: So, where is your grandpa now?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He went off on a new journey, and it's been quite a while since I last saw him.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: So, where has Clockie gone...? Did he leave to protect Dreamville?
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I heard some noises from the room... Origami Bird? That's a friend of mine.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: You and Origami Bird are friends?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, it's a member of the Compass crew, just like Clockie and Miss Mirror. And there's more than just one Origami Bird! They are a big family with lots of brothers and sisters who look the same.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: They follow Miss Mirror's orders and handle all sorts of jobs on the ship. They're the best sailors.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Sailors? Can Origami Birds be sailors...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Could you tell us more about the "Compass," Misha?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The "Compass" is a ship bound for the New World! Clockie and his partners travel through layers of fog to the depths of the sea. Whenever there is danger, Clockie will use a compass and guide the ship in the right direction!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: That's a great story, but in the Penacony cartoon, Clockie and his partners have always lived in Dreamville and never ventured out, right?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Huh? Oh... that does seem to be the case.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Weird... I clearly remember... Clockie arrived in the New World in the end...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Perhaps Clockie has a hidden past.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I think I hear the sound of water...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: [Trailblazer] once mentioned there's a magnificent fountain up ahead.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Look, there it is.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "The water resembles a precious jewel, embedded in the dreams of all seafarers."
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: "Every time I gaze at the shimmering lights beneath the waves, it feels as though I'm back in this place, standing by your side..."
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Have you recalled anything, Misha?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, I saw these sentences in Grandpa's logbook. He used to say that despite the perils of the sea, whenever he stood on the deck in the afternoon, overlooking the sparkling waves, he would think of this fountain in front of his house.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: He often said that those moments felt like returning to his family's side, and the difficulties at sea didn't seem quite as challenging.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: *sigh* You know, I quite understand such sentiments...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, don't tease! I was just being a bit sentimental.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm not an elder. I was just being a bit sentimental.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Perhaps every adventurer far from home carries a fountain within their soul. Even though the other side of the sea remains shrouded in the unknown, the fountain in front of his house serves as a compass, leading him back to his cherished ones.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, while Grandpa was at home, we would stand by the fountain and place the "Compass" — a toy boat that I made — into the pool!
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Back then, I would ask him when I could go on adventures like him, and he would always laugh and say I was still too young.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: It seems this "Mikhail" is truly a seafarer and has nothing to do with the Watchmaker.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, based on Misha's recollections, the scenes in the dream bubble appear to be his childhood memories.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: He didn't want me to call him "Grandpa" because that would make him sound old. He believed he was still young. The name "Mikhail" was given to him by his parents, Mihaly and Elise, both renowned seafarers.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: But this raises more questions. According to Misha, he was clearly born on an oceanic planet and led an ordinary life, with no connection to Penacony at all...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Could this be some sort of metaphor? Perhaps the "sea" refers to the Memory Zone?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm sorry. I don't know, but my memories keep pouring out uncontrollably, like water flowing from a fountain...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Perhaps... I'll remember more things if we go further...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: We're going to the opposite side, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, we should turn left here...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Huh? Something feels different about this place?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is it. I remember this corridor.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Up ahead is... Grandpa's study. It was in that room that I saw him the last time.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: The atmosphere in this room feels totally different.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Misha! You've finally come!
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Clockie, you're here! Yeah, this is the room where we first met each other...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Are those books on the bookshelf logbooks left behind by that seafarer?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, whenever he came back, he'd place a logbook on the bookshelf in his room. They contain records of his expeditions to every corner of the world.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: He described our world as a fountain. At some point, the sea started to gradually swallow up the land where people lived.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: To ensure that everyone had land to settle on, he had to continue exploring the sea and search for the source of the rising seawater.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: On that day, he called me to his study, telling me that he was embarking on another journey. However, I could sense the gravity in his expression. It... It was the same look I had seen on my father's face before his final voyage.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I asked him if I could go with him, but he said that my adventure lay elsewhere and told me to stay home and patiently await a certain sound at the door.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: What sound?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He told me about a vast ocean in the sky — an ocean of stars. He spoke of a train that transports children with a desire to venture far away, traversing the sea of stars without ever stopping.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: He said that he knew the crew on the train, and that he had asked them to take me along. He said the journey I had always dreamed of... would start there.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: A train? Could it be...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's the Astral Express. I remember now, Grandpa's friends are a group of Nameless who came to this world to resolve a disaster caused by a star.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Then he gave his pocket watch to me. It was his cherished treasure, appearing in every one of his adventure tales. He explained that difficult times were ahead but assured me that the watch would guide me.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: He said, as long as I kept moving forward, I'd eventually reach my desired destination. And then, it was as if I heard...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: The distant sound of a train whistle, echoing throughout the room...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Exactly, Misha! And then we followed that whistle, didn't we?
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Yeah, I think I can still find the way we took back then.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: This is the Dream Jigsaw, right? So, we're supposed to find the exit? But where can we find the last piece...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do you remember, [Trailblazer]? You said you obtained a mysterious shard when you stumbled into this place.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (Check the inventory.)
Hey, the shape seems to match. So, this shard is also connected to Misha?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like we're just one step from revealing the truth. Let's get to the other side and investigate.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: This is it. This... is my room of clocks.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: While I spent my time waiting for Grandpa to return from his voyage, Walder gave me this workshop, and it became my "secret base"...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Here, I learned how to repair clockwork and gears out of my fondness of precision mechanics. In my dreams, I was the captain of the "Compass," embarking on adventures with my companions, Clockie and Miss Mirror, in search of the New World.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I... I was born and raised here.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: So, this building in the dream bubble is your childhood "home."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yes, but not exactly. To be more precise...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: This "dream bubble" itself is my home.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: Looks like you've remembered everything now.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Wait, wait! Why does it feel like everyone else knows something I don't?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, the little guy here, right? But we all saw him in Dreamflux Reef, right? And Mr. Yang even greeted him.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like everyone on the Astral Express has a childlike spirit!
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: The answer lies in the Astral Express. [Trailblazer]'s experience shows that neither Firefly nor Acheron can see this Clockie.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And when we were in Dreamflux Reef, you may have noticed that for some reason, nobody outside of the Crew... had ever talked with Clockie.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In that case, it's unanimous.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In that case, it's unanimous.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A memetic life that can only be seen by a select few... It's just like a hidden message... left by someone for the Nameless.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But Misha can see Clockie, too, right? They even grew up together, but Misha hasn't started the way of the Trailblaze yet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the key to the mystery, March. Now, take a moment to recall...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Have you ever seen anyone outside of the Crew interact with Misha?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Wait... no way...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the answer, March 7th. This dream bubble is the place where I was born, and I... I'm a dweller in this dream just like a Memory Zone Meme.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I should have stayed here and waited for you, but when reality and memories merged, I unconsciously pushed open that door and left the bubble with Clockie.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: So, it's not that the Watchmaker's dream bubble is empty, but rather... the stuff inside ran away?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: And the whistle you heard was the sound of the Express arriving at Penacony?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's one way to see it, but I believe there is a longer story behind all this. It's best for Misha himself to explain all the details...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: How about we start with your name? Now, should we call you Misha? Or...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Thank you all for helping me rediscover my true self. Now, please allow me to reintroduce myself.
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: I was born on Lushaka in the Przesmir system, adopted by seafarers Mikhail and Char. They gave me a treasure, a name that carried their hopes...
rows.speaker: Misha

rows.text: If you prefer, you can call me by a more familiar name, the Watchmaker.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: So, you're the Watchmaker himself?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Unfortunately, that legendary figure is no more. I'm only a reflection of his life.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: Where are you going, Legwork? It's time to head to our next stop.
rows.speaker: "Navigator" Granholm

rows.text: As for the child who has been with you, he's the innocent protagonist of Misha's childhood dream, a friend of Clockie, a young apprentice, and a future mechanic on the Express...
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: And this also marks the beginning of his journey devoted to the Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: At the end of the journey, I left this little flame, which I so cherished, in my deepest dreams, hoping to pass it on to the Nameless of future generations.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: However, he somehow left the dream bubble and forgot all about his task. I apologize for all the confusion this caused.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: Because he was born with a desire to "trailblaze," wasn't he?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I don't think Misha has forgotten his role as a guide. He remembered it, and that's why he mistakenly appeared as a hotel {RUBY_B#bellboy}doorman{RUBY_E#} in [Trailblazer]'s dream from the very beginning.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The one who brought our unconscious [Trailblazer] here must have been Misha. If that's the case, we encountered the Watchmaker's Legacy from the beginning, didn't we?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Well, I have a sarcastic friend who says I always take big detours and end up back where I started... Perhaps that's what every Nameless has to go through.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: But in the end, you've found me. I'm sure you're all wondering what my legacy is. I believe my hound has mentioned the Stellaron and my wealth...
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: If I may apologize, the Stellaron part is real. As for my wealth, however, it's nothing more than a baseless rumor.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: I left my homeland as a child and embarked on the journey of Trailblaze. I traveled to various planets until finally reaching Asdana, where my friends and I built the original Penacony and fought for its future ever since...
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: I've been moving forward all my life, doing what I could to overcome the obstacles in my path. But ultimately, my journey reached its end, and I left behind no possessions worth entrusting...
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: So, if you ask what's left within this worn-out train engine that can be called a "legacy"... I suppose it's the things that are still burning in the engine's furnace.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: Now that you're well aware of the current situation of Penacony, I certainly hope that you'll help me get this world back on track. But I'll leave that decision to you, for the Path of Trailblaze is never paved by others.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: All I have for you is a story and two gifts...
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: I want to give you my pocket watch. It has accompanied me throughout my long journey, guiding that naive child forward, and has been blessed with the presence of so many great people up to this day.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: And my hat, too. The one who navigated for me placed it on my head and planted a fanciful thought in my mind — the Trailblazing expedition will never end.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: Now, it's time for you to make your choice. Once you've made up your mind, open that door and enter the long dream of an old man.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: I'll be waiting for you at the end of this corridor of time.
rows.speaker: "The Watchmaker"

rows.text: All right, everyone. Let's make a decision.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Although I don't think anyone will have any objections.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Come on... Stop joking at a moment like this. We've come this far. Surely there's no other option than moving forward.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: In that case, the vote stands at two to one.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Then let's proceed together to the end of this dream... and tell Mikhail our decision.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Mikhail! Where are you going...?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Someone has to step up and save Lushaka. So, why can't it be me, Misha?
rows.speaker: "Seafarer" Mikhail

rows.text: Please, don't go. And if you must, please take me with you... Don't leave me alone...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Even without me, you know how to proceed forward, brave Captain Misha. The "Compass" is waiting for you. Haven't you always wanted to be a better adventurer than me?
rows.speaker: "Seafarer" Mikhail

rows.text: Now go. Board that train and... start your journey.
rows.speaker: "Seafarer" Mikhail

rows.text: Where are you going, Mikhail?
rows.speaker: Navigator Falcon Amundsen

rows.text: I... I'm going to clean the floor in the Parlor Car! I've promised the conductor...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Wait, first tell me, did you fix this watch?
rows.speaker: Navigator Falcon Amundsen

rows.text: Um... yeah.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I know what it looked like before. Its chain was broken, the back case torn, and the marks on the dial all worn out... How did you manage to fix it?
rows.speaker: Navigator Falcon Amundsen

rows.text: Well... It's hard to explain, but I knew it could be fixed...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: It's the hands, Mr. Amundsen. Its hands were intact and pointing in the right direction, so I knew there would be a way to fix the rest.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I see, you'll work with me from now on. Haven't you always wanted to tinker with this train? You're its mechanic now. As for the conductor, I'll do the talking.
rows.speaker: Navigator Falcon Amundsen

rows.text: B—But I only know how to fix watches...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Don't worry, you've got what it takes. I'll teach you what you need to know.
rows.speaker: Navigator Falcon Amundsen

rows.text: I... I'm staying in Asdana, with Razalina and Tiernan.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I see... This place reminds you of home?
rows.speaker: "Navigator" Granholm

rows.text: The people of Asdana have only achieved a tiny victory and still have a long way to go... towards true freedom. Hanunue needs us.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Don't worry, not all journeys lead to the stars. Even if I leave the Express, our Path of Trailblaze will continue.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Yeah, I knew you wouldn't stay on the Express forever. Leave in peace, my friend, and take this with you.
rows.speaker: "Navigator" Granholm

rows.text: This is... Mr. Amundsen's hat? But why...?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: When he departed, he said he would leave it to his best student. Well, I suppose the time has come.
rows.speaker: "Navigator" Granholm

rows.text: Farewell, Legwork. Take care of Tiernan and Razalina, and don't forget to... write to us.
rows.speaker: "Navigator" Granholm

rows.text: Where are you going, Watchmaker?
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: Don't worry, Micah. Just going on a little trip.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Someone has to be at the forefront of the interstellar frontier, and I'm the only former Nameless in Penacony. So, why can't it be me?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Because you're all we have! Have you forgotten about Tiernan? The Cosmos is way more dangerous now! What will happen to Penacony if we lose you, too?
rows.speaker: Micah

rows.text: But what will happen to Penacony if we don't find a way out?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Tiernan... How could I ever forget him? I've spent countless sleepless nights asking myself why I didn't go with him back then.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: We Nameless won't stop... Don't worry, Micah, it's just a matter of getting back to my old profession. Just wait for me to come back. But if, and it's a big if...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: If I don't come back in one piece, then you'll become the next Watchmaker.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Where are you going, old man?
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Oh, you're here.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Answer my question. What are you up to?
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Relax, Gallagher. I just came up with a great idea. Wanna hear it?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Oh, come on! Aren't all your "ideas" just ways to get yourself killed? I may be blunt here, but you're the last remaining hero in Penacony.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: If you die too, the secret of the Stellaron... will go to the grave with you.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Yes, I'm afraid there's no way out in Penacony, so I'll have to consider alternatives beyond Asdana.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: We'll organize a festival, using the "Watchmaker's Legacy" as a facade... and send invitations to the entire Cosmos to gather people here.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: So? A desperate struggle against The Family?
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: Desperate? Hah, don't we have you here, my friend? This task is challenging, but what hasn't been challenging for us along the way? Well, whatever you do, remember...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Make sure to send an invitation to the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Misha! Where are you going?
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Oh, it's you, Clockie... Take me to Dreamflux Reef...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Last night, I had a long dream about the day we met. I want to write down that dream.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Write it down... Why?
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: So I won't forget it. Do you remember how you got your name, Clockie?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Of course! You told me that when you were a kid, you lived in a room full of clocks. Those wall clocks and pocket watches grew up with you and were your best friends!
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Yes, but what I didn't mention was... there's a funny misunderstanding behind it.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I was a kid, and there was always a special pocket watch in my memories. It was with my grandpa, guiding him on his sea voyages and leading the way in his every adventure story.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I wanted to have a pocket watch like that too, and that's when you appeared in my dreams.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Yeah, every night we boarded the Compass and set sail together!
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Mikhail Char Legwork, or simply... {RUBY_B#Mikhail-Char}Misha{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: But you know what? It wasn't until the day my grandpa gave it to me that I realized... it wasn't a pocket watch at all...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: It was a compass.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: So, your name should have been "Compassie"...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: And the Watchmaker... is just a Nameless.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: We've arrived at Dreamflux Reef. So, where to next?
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: You know, Clockie. I don't think... I'll be going anywhere else.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I've traveled far enough, and it's time for a little break...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Oh, so we'll set out again when you're rested?
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: No, I'll stay here, and then... this is where it ends.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: This is where it ends? What do you mean, Misha?
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: You told me that the Trailblazing expedition would never end.
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Yeah, that's what I said...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: So now, it's up to you to decide your next destination.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: My next destination? What's that supposed to be? I've been following you...
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Misha? You're acting weird today! If you're feeling down, we can just do what we usually do... with the clockwork!
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: No, I'm not feeling down. As for clockwork... yeah, it resolves all problems in this dream.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: So, do you know what clockwork actually is?
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Hmm? I'm not quite sure.
rows.speaker: Clockie

rows.text: Well, everyone gets lost at times. They may hesitate and doubt which way to go. That happens in this Dreamscape and beyond.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: But don't worry, everyone goes through moments of uncertainty and hesitation. Eventually, they gather the courage to make bold decisions...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Whether it's calming, happy, angry, or sad, all they need is a little nudge to take that step toward where they truly belong.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I'm leaving that little nudge with you, and I hope you'll share it with others...
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: Such is the essence of clockwork, the will of the Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: Mikhail Char Legwork

rows.text: I can't believe {RUBY_B#Xipe, the Harmony}that Aeon{RUBY_E#} would cast a glance at Penacony at a time like this... Is it because of the resonance from the legacy of the Trailblaze? Or perhaps the bond between you is so strong that it even impresses an Aeon?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Well, there might be another possibility. Perhaps THEY want to witness, on behalf of the {RUBY_B#Akivili and Ena}fallen Aeons{RUBY_E#}, who will hold the future of Penacony.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If that's the case, on behalf of the Dreammaster of Penacony and the 107,336 members of the Oak Family, I'm extending a formal invitation to all of you...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm cordially inviting you all to the Penacony Grand Theater to participate in the upcoming Charmony Festival. And of course, you won't be in the audience, but on center stage.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Since the future of the Stellaron, Penacony, and even the entire Cosmos is at stake, let's draw a conclusion there, in all fairness.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: If you truly believe in {RUBY_B#Aeon of Trailblaze}Akivili's{RUBY_E#} path, then show me THEIR courage and determination.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Does that mean he wants to fight us during the Charmony Festival?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm afraid so.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: This is weird! Aren't arch villains usually plotting some dirty conspiracy in the end? But he actually said something like "in all fairness"... Could it be that he's underestimating us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What happened to the Grand Theater stage?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, in my opinion, Sunday is deeply committed to his own philosophy and genuinely wants to prove that the Order is right.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I sensed a strong conviction and a desire for dominance in him. Maybe he won't accept the outcome unless he wins fair and square.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That's why he'll give it his all in the upcoming battle.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, you're right! We've even dealt with a Lord Ravager of the Destruction, so a follower of the Order won't be a big deal!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A—Are you backing out now!? We've even dealt with a Lord Ravager of the Destruction, so a follower of the Order won't be a big deal!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You...! Every time an important moment arrives, you hesitate.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We've even dealt with a Lord Ravager of the Destruction, so a follower of the Order won't be a big deal!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Anyway, we can't leave the Stellaron unchecked. This is about trailblazing a bright future for Penacony and fulfilling Mikhail's and his predecessors' long-cherished wishes.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Now that we've taken up the mantle, we can't afford to fail them.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: However, the same applies to the Order. Their plan didn't materialize overnight, and they have the profound collective consciousness of the Planet of Festivities behind them...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: A desire to dream, to slumber and escape reality... All those hidden emotions have given birth to the sweet dream of the Order.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: They've harnessed the will of an entire planet to create an Aeon... This confrontation is far more complicated than a simple power struggle. To secure Penacony's future, fighting on the stage alone is not enough.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: What do you mean? Are you not coming with us...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I believe Firefly is trying to say that she's heading off to another battle.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Mhmm.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: ...Before I left, Destiny's Slave told me that this journey would bring unforgettable rewards. Even though the script he gave me only had a few lines, I couldn't ignore them.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Because one of the lines said... I'll experience "death" three times in the land of the dreams.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Three times!? This can't be serious, right...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The first time was a painful death when I was stabbed by the blade of "Dormancy," which led to all subsequent events. The script will always come true, but in a way... that will only be revealed when that page is turned.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: So now, I've understood the meaning of my second "death," and I am prepared to face it. If all goes well, my efforts will provide crucial support for you.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Only by achieving victory in this battle can we secure a future for Penacony. And only then, my third and final death... won't come true in the most terrible form.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The most terrible form? Does that mean...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The true "death"... where everyone in Penacony loses themselves completely in the eternal sweet dream of the Order.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: "Accountant! We are the pillars of this mansion, bound by an oath of loyalty and unity... Why are you plotting my downfall?"
rows.speaker: Merchant

rows.text: "Because Master shaped you from clay but forged me from fire! I'm superior to you!"
rows.speaker: Accountant

rows.text: "The Blackplum Family was the first to fall. They withered away in the White Desert event orchestrated by the Alfalfa Family."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: We must do everything we can to prevent that.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Have you... made up your mind, Firefly?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yes, otherwise I wouldn't be here.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Thank you again for your assistance for the Astral Express. May we meet again in reality.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, farewell, everyone. May your Trailblazing expedition never end.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: After today, Jepella's name will disappear from cosmic history, and the Ever-Flame Mansion will take its place. In the not-too-distant future, you'll receive an invitation...
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: That's your next stop.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Land of the Dreams, Penacony.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: I hope you find whatever you seek there, be it answers... or salvation.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: You mean... my three "deaths"?
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Silver Wolf told me about it. It's such a shame that it's not part of my script.
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: While I want to live, I'm never afraid of death. The opposite of death is eternal life, and that's... that's something I'll never desire.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: People die, and I am no exception. Death is like a script, a fate that cannot be defied. But that's exactly why...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: We have to choose where we want to rest forever.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Do you exist just to perish?
rows.speaker: Blade

rows.text: Are you not the same, Blade? The end you desire is not one dictated by others.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: If I were to die now, I would only be a weapon. I believe... I should die as a human.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Though its definition escapes me, isn't this the answer that ordinary people look for their whole lives? A name that can be carved onto their tombstone.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: The world is in harmony and the stars shine bright. Praise the Great One!
rows.speaker: Crowd's Cheers

rows.text: The Order is dead! The Order is dead! The Order is dead!
rows.speaker: Crowd's Cheers

rows.text: The tombstone that belongs to me once bore the inscription "Glamoth's Iron Cavalry," then it changed to "Stellaron Hunter," but one day...
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: It will bear the name "Firefly" and the brilliance she showed at the end of her life.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: That's quite unexpected, old man. Who would've thought your crazy plan would actually work? Do all you Nameless fools just act on a whim?
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: "I wish they could {RUBY_B#calm down}regain their reason{RUBY_E#} and cast away the shackles of hypocrisy," proclaimed the new master.
I can sense that this false sweet dream is coming to an end. The Nameless may be young, but they had the ability to achieve this goal... just like you did in your time.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: "Only {RUBY_B#calmness}reason{RUBY_E#} can shield people from the lingering poison of the past," proclaimed the new master.
It's a shame you won't be able to see it firsthand. Heh, maybe I won't either... Once something {RUBY_B#Fictionologist}fictional{RUBY_E#} is seen through, it ceases to exist.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: "Only the calmed ones can evade the insidious influence of the hidden instigator," proclaimed the new master.

Yeah, not just those Nameless, even Mr. Wings is just like you... Stubborn, won't listen or give up, no matter what... Well, fate is unpredictable, I guess. If we weren't bound by those cursed Paths, maybe we could've had some good talks.
rows.speaker: Gallagher

rows.text: "In the absence of calmness, there exists no path to liberation from the clutches of death," proclaimed the new master.
